\displaystyle m=O\left(\frac{C_{\texttt{cov},\gamma}\log(\lvert\Pi\rvert\rho^{-1})\log(\delta^{-1})}{\delta\epsilon^{2}}\right).

Proof of Appendix I. Under realizability of $\pi^{\texttt{BoN}}_{N}$ (Section 4.1), Section F.2 implies that the output of SFT-Sharpening satisfies, with probability at least $1-\rho$,

\displaystyle\En_{x\sim\mu}\left[D^{2}_{\mathsf{H}}\left(\widehat{\pi}(\cdot\mid{}x),\pi^{\texttt{BoN}}_{N}(\cdot\mid{}x)\right)\right]\leq\varepsilon_{\texttt{stat}}^{2}\vcentcolon={}\frac{2\log(\lvert\Pi\rvert/\rho)}{n}.

Henceforth we condition on the event that Eq. 108 holds. Let

\mathcal{X}_{\texttt{good}}\vcentcolon={}\left\{x\in\mathcal{X}\mid N^{\star}\geq\frac{1}{\pi_{\texttt{base}}(\bm{y}^{\star}_{\gamma}(x)\mid{}x)}\right\}

denote the set of prompts for which $\pi_{\texttt{base}}$ places sufficiently high mass on $\bm{y}^{\star}_{\gamma}(x)$. We can bound

\displaystyle\mathbb{P}_{x\sim\mu}\left[\widehat{\pi}(\bm{y}^{\star}_{\gamma}(x)\mid{}x)\leq{}1-\delta\right] \displaystyle\qquad\leq{}\mathbb{P}_{x\sim\mu}\left[\widehat{\pi}(\bm{y}^{\star}_{\gamma}(x)\mid{}x)\leq{}1-\delta,x\in\mathcal{X}_{\texttt{good}}\right]+\mathbb{P}_{x\sim\mu}\left[x\notin\mathcal{X}_{\texttt{good}}\right].

To bound the first term in Eq. 111, note that if $x\in\mathcal{X}_{\texttt{good}}$, then $\pi^{\texttt{BoN}}_{N}(\bm{y}^{\star}_{\gamma}(x)\mid{}x)\geq{}1-\delta/2$. Indeed, observe that $y\sim\pi^{\texttt{BoN}}_{N}(\cdot\mid{}x)\notin\bm{y}^{\star}_{\gamma}(x)$ if and only if $y_{1},\ldots,y_{N}\sim\pi_{\texttt{base}}(x)$ have $y_{i}\notin\bm{y}^{\star}_{\gamma}(x)$ for all $i$, which happens with probability $(1-\pi_{\texttt{base}}(\bm{y}^{\star}_{\gamma}(x)\mid{}x))^{N}\leq(1-1/N^{\star})^{N}\leq\delta/2$ since $x\in\mathcal{X}_{\texttt{good}}$. It follows that for any such $x$, we can lower bound (using the data processing inequality)

\displaystyle D^{2}_{\mathsf{H}}\left(\widehat{\pi}(\cdot\mid{}x),\pi^{\texttt{BoN}}_{N}(\cdot\mid{}x)\right) \displaystyle\geq\left(\sqrt{1-\widehat{\pi}(\bm{y}^{\star}_{\gamma}(x)\mid{}x)}-\sqrt{1-\pi^{\texttt{BoN}}_{N}(\bm{y}^{\star}_{\gamma}(x)\mid{}x)}\right)^{2} \displaystyle\gtrsim{}\delta\cdot\mathbb{I}\left\{\widehat{\pi}(\bm{y}^{\star}_{\gamma}(x)\mid{}x)\leq{}1-\delta\right\}.

By Eqs. 108 and 113, it follows that

\mathbb{P}_{x\sim\mu}\left[\widehat{\pi}(\bm{y}^{\star}_{\gamma}(x)\mid{}x)\leq{}1-\delta,x\in\mathcal{X}_{\texttt{good}}\right]\lesssim\frac{\varepsilon_{\texttt{stat}}^{2}}{\delta}.

For the second term in Eq. 111, we bound

\displaystyle\mathbb{P}_{x\sim\mu}\left[x\notin\mathcal{X}_{\texttt{good}}\right] \displaystyle=\mathbb{P}_{x\sim\mu}\left[N^{\star}<\frac{1}{\pi_{\texttt{base}}(\bm{y}^{\star}_{\gamma}(x)\mid{}x)}\right] \displaystyle=\mathbb{P}_{x\sim\mu}\left[\frac{1}{N^{\star}\pi_{\texttt{base}}(\bm{y}^{\star}_{\gamma}(x)\mid{}x)}>1\right] \displaystyle\leq{}\frac{1}{N^{\star}}\En_{x\sim\mu}\left[\frac{1}{\pi_{\texttt{base}}(\bm{y}^{\star}_{\gamma}(x)\mid{}x)}\right] \displaystyle\leq{}\frac{C_{\texttt{cov},\gamma}}{N^{\star}}

via Markov’s inequality and the definition of $C_{\texttt{cov},\gamma}$. Substituting both bounds into Eq. 111 completes the proof. ∎

Proof of Appendix D. The proof begins similarly to Section 4.1. By realizability of $\pi_{N_{\mu}}$, Section F.2 implies that the output of SFT-Sharpening satisfies, with probability at least $1-\rho$,

\displaystyle\En_{x\sim\mu}\left[D^{2}_{\mathsf{H}}\left(\widehat{\pi}(\cdot\mid{}x),\pi_{N_{\mu}}(\cdot\mid{}x)\right)\right]\leq\varepsilon_{\texttt{stat}}^{2}\vcentcolon={}\frac{2\log(\lvert\Pi\rvert/\rho)}{n}.

Condition on the event that this guarantee holds. We invoke the following lemma, proven in the sequel. Let $P$ be a distribution on a discrete space $\mathcal{Y}$. Let $\bm{y}^{\star}=\argmax_{y\in\mathcal{Y}}P(y)$ and let $P^{\star}:=\max_{y\in\mathcal{Y}}P(y)$. Let $y_{1},y_{2},\ldots\sim{}P$, and for any stopping time $\tau$, define

\displaystyle\widehat{y}_{\tau}\in\argmax\left\{P(y):y\in\left\{y_{1},\dots,y_{\tau}\right\}\right\}.

Next, for a parameter $\mu>0$, define the stopping time

\displaystyle N_{\mu}:=\inf\left\{k:\frac{1}{\max_{1\leq i\leq k}P(y_{i})}\leq k/\mu\right\}.

Then

\displaystyle\En[N_{\mu}]\leq\frac{\mu+(1/|\bm{y}^{\star}|)}{P^{\star}}.

In addition, for any stopping time $\tau\geq N_{\mu}$ (including $\tau=N_{\mu}$ itself), we have $\mathbb{P}[\widehat{y}_{\tau}\notin\bm{y}^{\star}]\leq e^{-\lvert\bm{y}^{\star}\rvert\mu}$. This lemma, with our choice of $\mu$, ensures that for all $x\in\mathcal{X}$,

\displaystyle\pi_{N_{\mu}}(\bm{y}^{\star}(x)\mid x)\geq 1-e^{-\mu}=1-\delta/2.

Following the reasoning in Eq. 113, this implies that

\displaystyle D^{2}_{\mathsf{H}}\left(\widehat{\pi}(\cdot\mid{}x),\pi_{N_{\mu}}(\cdot\mid{}x)\right)\gtrsim{}\delta\cdot\mathbb{I}\left\{\widehat{\pi}(\bm{y}^{\star}(x)\mid{}x)\leq{}1-\delta\right\},

so that

\displaystyle\mathbb{P}_{x\sim\mu}\left[\widehat{\pi}(\bm{y}^{\star}(x)\mid{}x)\leq{}1-\delta\right]\lesssim\frac{\varepsilon_{\texttt{stat}}^{2}}{\delta}

as desired.

To bound the expected sample complexity, we observe that

\displaystyle\En[m]=n\cdot\En[N_{\mu}(x)]\overset{(i)}{\leq}\En\left[\frac{1+\mu}{\pi_{\texttt{base}}(\bm{y}^{\star}(x)\mid x)}\right]=(1+\mu)\macc@depth\char 1\relax\macc@set@skewchar\macc@nested@a 111{C}_{\texttt{cov}},

where inequality $(i)$ invokes Appendix I once more. ∎

Proof of Appendix I. Define $N^{\star}:=\mu/P^{\star}$. To bound the tails of $N_{\mu}$, define

\displaystyle\tau=\inf\{k\mid{}k\geq N^{\star}\text{ and }\bm{y}^{\star}\cap\{y_{1},\dots,y_{k}\}\neq\varnothing\}.

It follows from the definition that $N_{\mu}\leq\tau$, since for any $k\geq{}N^{\star}$, if there exists $i\leq{}k$ such that $y_{i}\in\bm{y}^{\star}$, then

\displaystyle\frac{1}{P(y_{i})}=\frac{1}{P^{\star}}=\frac{N^{\star}}{\mu}\leq\frac{k}{\mu}.

Thus, for $k\geq N^{\star}$, we can bound

\displaystyle\mathbb{P}[N_{\mu}>k]\leq\mathbb{P}[\tau>k]=\mathbb{P}[\mathcal{Y}^{\star}\cap\{y_{1},\dots,y_{k}\}=\varnothing]\leq(1-|\bm{y}^{\star}|P^{\star})^{k},

and consequently

\displaystyle\En[N_{\mu}]\leq\En[\tau] \displaystyle\leq\En[\tau\mathbb{I}\{\tau\leq N^{\star}\}]+\En[\tau\mathbb{I}\{\tau>N^{\star}\}] \displaystyle\leq N^{\star}+\sum_{k>N^{\star}}(1-|\bm{y}^{\star}|P^{\star})^{k} \displaystyle\leq N^{\star}+\frac{1}{|\bm{y}^{\star}|P(y^{\star})}=\frac{\mu+1/|\bm{y}^{\star}|}{P(y^{\star})}.

To prove correctness, observe that $N_{\mu}\geq N^{\star}$, because for all $y\in\mathcal{Y}$, $\frac{1}{P(y)}\geq N^{\star}/\mu$. Hence, any stopping time $\tau\geq N_{\mu}$ also satisfies $\tau\geq N^{\star}$, and moreover has $\widehat{y}_{\tau}\in\bm{y}^{\star}$ whenever $\bm{y}^{\star}\cap\{y_{1},y_{2},\dots,y_{\tau}\}\neq\varnothing$. This fails to occur with probability no more than

\displaystyle\left(1-\frac{|\bm{y}^{\star}|}{P^{\star}}\right)^{N^{\star}}=\left(1-\frac{|\bm{y}^{\star}|}{P^{\star}}\right)^{\mu/P^{\star}}\leq e^{-|\bm{y}^{\star}|\mu}.

∎

sections.title: J.1 Proof of Section 4.2.1

paragraphs.text: We state and prove a generalized version of Section 4.2.1. In the assumptions below, we fix a parameter $\gamma\in[0,1)$; the setting $\gamma=0$ corresponds to Section 4.2.1.

[Coverage] All $\pi\in\Pi$ satisfy $\mathcal{C}_{\pi}\leq C_{\texttt{conc}}$ for a parameter $C_{\texttt{conc}}\geq(1-\gamma)^{-1}C_{\texttt{cov},\gamma}$, and $\mathcal{C}_{\nicefrac{{\pi_{\texttt{base}}}}{{\pi}};\beta}\leq C_{\texttt{loss}}$ for a parameter $C_{\texttt{loss}}\geq\lvert\mathcal{Y}\rvert$. By Section J.1.1, Section J.1 is consistent with the assumption that $\pi^{\star}_{\beta}\in\Pi$.
[Margin] For all $x\in\mathrm{supp}(\mu)$, the initial model $\pi_{\texttt{base}}$ satisfies
\pi_{\texttt{base}}(\bm{y}^{\star}_{\gamma}(x)\mid{}x)\geq{}(1+\gamma_{\mathsf{margin}})\cdot\pi_{\texttt{base}}(y\mid{}x)\quad\forall{}y\not\in\bm{y}^{\star}_{\gamma}(x)
for a parameter $\gamma_{\mathsf{margin}}>0$.

Assume that $\pi^{\star}_{\beta}\in\Pi$ (Section 4.2.1), and that Section 4.2.1 and Section 4.2 hold with respect to some $\gamma\in[0,1)$, with parameters $C_{\texttt{conc}}$, $C_{\texttt{loss}}$, and $\gamma_{\mathsf{margin}}>0$. For any $\delta,\rho\in(0,1)$, the DPO algorithm in Eq. 7 ensures that with probability at least $1-\rho$,

\displaystyle\mathbb{P}_{x\sim\mu}\left[\widehat{\pi}(\bm{y}^{\star}_{\gamma}(x)\mid{}x)\leq{}1-\delta\right]\lesssim{}\frac{1}{\gamma_{\mathsf{margin}}\delta}\cdot{}\widetilde{O}\left(\sqrt{\frac{C_{\texttt{conc}}\log^{3}(C_{\texttt{loss}}\lvert\Pi\rvert\rho^{-1})}{n}}+\beta\log(C_{\texttt{conc}})+\gamma\right)
where $\widetilde{O}\left(\cdot\right)$ hides factors logarithmic in $n$ and $C_{\texttt{conc}}$ and doubly logarithmic in $\Pi$, $C_{\texttt{loss}}$, and $\rho^{-1}$.
We first state and prove some supporting technical lemmas, then proceed to the proof of Section J.1.

sections.title: J.1.1 Technical lemmas

paragraphs.text: The following result is a generalization of Section 4.2.1.

For all $\gamma\in(0,1)$, the model $\pi^{\star}_{\beta}$ satisfies $\mathcal{C}_{\pi^{\star}_{\beta}}\leq(1-\gamma)^{-1}C_{\texttt{cov},\gamma}$ and $\mathcal{C}_{\nicefrac{{\pi_{\texttt{base}}}}{{\pi^{\star}_{\beta}}};\beta}\leq{}\left\lvert\mathcal{Y}\right\rvert$.
Proof of Section J.1.1. For any fixed $x\in\mathcal{X}$, we have

\displaystyle\En_{y\sim\pi^{\star}_{\beta}(\cdot\mid x)}\left[\frac{\pi^{\star}_{\beta}(y\mid x)}{\pi_{\texttt{base}}(y\mid x)}\right] \displaystyle=\En_{y\sim\pi^{\star}_{\beta}(\cdot\mid x)}\left[\frac{\pi_{\texttt{base}}^{1+\beta^{-1}}(y\mid{}x)}{\pi_{\texttt{base}}(y\mid{}x)}\right]\cdot{}\left(\sum_{y^{\prime}\in\mathcal{Y}}\pi_{\texttt{base}}^{1+\beta^{-1}}(y^{\prime}\mid{}x)\right)^{-1} \displaystyle\leq{}\max_{y\in\mathcal{Y}}\pi_{\texttt{base}}^{\beta^{-1}}(y\mid{}x)\cdot{}\left(\sum_{y^{\prime}\in\mathcal{Y}}\pi_{\texttt{base}}^{1+\beta^{-1}}(y^{\prime}\mid{}x)\right)^{-1} \displaystyle\leq{}(1-\gamma)^{-1}\pi_{\texttt{base}}^{\beta^{-1}}(\bm{y}^{\star}_{\gamma}(x)\mid{}x)\cdot{}\left(\sum_{y^{\prime}\in\mathcal{Y}}\pi_{\texttt{base}}^{1+\beta^{-1}}(y^{\prime}\mid{}x)\right)^{-1} \displaystyle=(1-\gamma)^{-1}\frac{\pi_{\texttt{base}}^{1+\beta^{-1}}(\bm{y}^{\star}_{\gamma}(x)\mid{}x)}{\pi_{\texttt{base}}(\bm{y}^{\star}_{\gamma}(x)\mid{}x)}\cdot{}\left(\sum_{y^{\prime}\in\mathcal{Y}}\pi_{\texttt{base}}^{1+\beta^{-1}}(y^{\prime}\mid{}x)\right)^{-1} \displaystyle=(1-\gamma)^{-1}\frac{\sum_{y\in\bm{y}^{\star}_{\gamma}(x)}\pi_{\texttt{base}}^{1+\beta^{-1}}(y\mid{}x)}{\pi_{\texttt{base}}(\bm{y}^{\star}_{\gamma}(x)\mid{}x)}\cdot{}\left(\sum_{y^{\prime}\in\mathcal{Y}}\pi_{\texttt{base}}^{1+\beta^{-1}}(y^{\prime}\mid{}x)\right)^{-1} \displaystyle\leq(1-\gamma)^{-1}\frac{1}{\pi_{\texttt{base}}(\bm{y}^{\star}_{\gamma}(x)\mid{}x)}.
It follows that $\mathcal{C}_{\pi^{\star}_{\beta}}\leq(1-\gamma)^{-1}C_{\texttt{cov},\gamma}$ as claimed.
For the second result, we have

\displaystyle\mathcal{C}_{\nicefrac{{\pi_{\texttt{base}}}}{{\pi^{\star}_{\beta}}};\beta}=\En_{\pi_{\texttt{base}}}\left[\frac{1}{\pi_{\texttt{base}}(y\mid{}x)}\cdot\left(\sum_{y^{\prime}\in\mathcal{Y}}\pi_{\texttt{base}}^{1+\beta^{-1}}(y^{\prime}\mid{}x)\right)^{\beta}\right]\leq{}\En_{\pi_{\texttt{base}}}\left[\frac{1}{\pi_{\texttt{base}}(y\mid{}x)}\right]=\lvert\mathcal{Y}\rvert.
The next lemmas provide bounds on the tails of the self-rewards used in the algorithm.
Suppose $\beta\in[0,1]$. For any model $\pi$, with probability at least $1-\delta$ over the draw of $x\sim\mu$, $y,y^{\prime}\sim\pi_{\texttt{base}}(\cdot\mid x)$, we have that for all $s>0$,

\displaystyle\mathbb{P}\left[\left\lvert\beta\log\left(\frac{\pi(y\mid{}x)}{\pi_{\texttt{base}}(y\mid{}x)}\right)-\beta\log\left(\frac{\pi(y^{\prime}\mid{}x)}{\pi_{\texttt{base}}(y^{\prime}\mid{}x)}\right)\right\rvert>\log(2\mathcal{C}_{\nicefrac{{\pi_{\texttt{base}}}}{{\pi}};\beta})+s\right]\leq\exp\left(-s\right).
Proof of Section J.1.1. Define

X\vcentcolon=\left\lvert\beta\log\left(\frac{\pi(y\mid{}x)}{\pi_{\texttt{base}}(y\mid{}x)}\right)-\beta\log\left(\frac{\pi(y^{\prime}\mid{}x)}{\pi_{\texttt{base}}(y^{\prime}\mid{}x)}\right)\right\rvert.
By the Chernoff method, we have that with probability at least $1-\delta$,

\displaystyle X \displaystyle\leq{}\log(\En\left[\exp(X)\right])+\log(\delta^{-1}) \displaystyle=\log\left(\En_{x\sim\mu,y,y^{\prime}\sim\pi_{\texttt{base}}(x)}\left[\exp\left(\left\lvert\beta\log\left(\frac{\pi(y\mid{}x)}{\pi_{\texttt{base}}(y\mid{}x)}\right)-\beta\log\left(\frac{\pi(y^{\prime}\mid{}x)}{\pi_{\texttt{base}}(y^{\prime}\mid{}x)}\right)\right\rvert\right)\right]\right)+\log(\delta^{-1}) \displaystyle\leq{}\log\Bigg(\En_{x\sim\mu,y,y^{\prime}\sim\pi_{\texttt{base}}(x)}\left[\exp\left(\beta\log\left(\frac{\pi(y\mid{}x)}{\pi_{\texttt{base}}(y\mid{}x)}\right)-\beta\log\left(\frac{\pi(y^{\prime}\mid{}x)}{\pi_{\texttt{base}}(y^{\prime}\mid{}x)}\right)\right)\right] \displaystyle\qquad+\En_{x\sim\mu,y,y^{\prime}\sim\pi_{\texttt{base}}(x)}\left[\exp\left(\beta\log\left(\frac{\pi(y^{\prime}\mid{}x)}{\pi_{\texttt{base}}(y^{\prime}\mid{}x)}\right)-\beta\log\left(\frac{\pi(y\mid{}x)}{\pi_{\texttt{base}}(y\mid{}x)}\right)\right)\right]\Bigg)+\log(\delta^{-1}) \displaystyle=\log\left(2\En_{x\sim\mu,y,y^{\prime}\sim\pi_{\texttt{base}}(x)}\left[\exp\left(\beta\log\left(\frac{\pi(y\mid{}x)}{\pi_{\texttt{base}}(y\mid{}x)}\right)-\beta\log\left(\frac{\pi(y^{\prime}\mid{}x)}{\pi_{\texttt{base}}(y^{\prime}\mid{}x)}\right)\right)\right]\right)+\log(\delta^{-1}) \displaystyle=\log\left(\En_{x\sim\mu,y,y^{\prime}\sim\pi_{\texttt{base}}(x)}\left[\left(\frac{\pi(y\mid{}x)}{\pi_{\texttt{base}}(y\mid{}x)}\cdot\frac{\pi_{\texttt{base}}(y^{\prime}\mid{}x)}{\pi(y^{\prime}\mid{}x)}\right)^{\beta}\right]\right)+\log(2\delta^{-1}).
As long as $\beta\leq{}1$, by Jensen’s inequality, we can bound

\displaystyle\En_{x\sim\mu,y,y^{\prime}\sim\pi_{\texttt{base}}(x)}\left[\left(\frac{\pi(y\mid{}x)}{\pi_{\texttt{base}}(y\mid{}x)}\cdot\frac{\pi_{\texttt{base}}(y^{\prime}\mid{}x)}{\pi(y^{\prime}\mid{}x)}\right)^{\beta}\right] \displaystyle\leq{}\En_{x\sim\mu,y^{\prime}\sim\pi_{\texttt{base}}(x)}\left[\left(\En_{y\sim\pi_{\texttt{base}}(x)}\left[\frac{\pi(y\mid{}x)}{\pi_{\texttt{base}}(y\mid{}x)}\right]\cdot\frac{\pi_{\texttt{base}}(y^{\prime}\mid{}x)}{\pi(y^{\prime}\mid{}x)}\right)^{\beta}\right] \displaystyle=\En_{x\sim\mu,y^{\prime}\sim\pi_{\texttt{base}}(x)}\left[\left(\frac{\pi_{\texttt{base}}(y^{\prime}\mid{}x)}{\pi(y^{\prime}\mid{}x)}\right)^{\beta}\right] \displaystyle=\mathcal{C}_{\nicefrac{{\pi_{\texttt{base}}}}{{\pi}};\beta},
which proves the result. ∎
Let $\beta\in[0,1]$. For all models $\pi$, we have

\displaystyle\En_{x\sim\mu,y,y^{\prime}\sim\pi_{\texttt{base}}(\cdot\mid x)}\left[\left\lvert\beta\log\left(\frac{\pi(y\mid{}x)}{\pi_{\texttt{base}}(y\mid{}x)}\right)-\beta\log\left(\frac{\pi(y^{\prime}\mid{}x)}{\pi_{\texttt{base}}(y^{\prime}\mid{}x)}\right)\right\rvert^{4}\right]\leq{}O(\log^{4}(\mathcal{C}_{\nicefrac{{\pi_{\texttt{base}}}}{{\pi}};\beta})+1).
Proof of Section J.1.1. Define

X\vcentcolon=\left\lvert\beta\log\left(\frac{\pi(y\mid{}x)}{\pi_{\texttt{base}}(y\mid{}x)}\right)-\beta\log\left(\frac{\pi(y^{\prime}\mid{}x)}{\pi_{\texttt{base}}(y^{\prime}\mid{}x)}\right)\right\rvert.
Set $k=\log(2\mathcal{C}_{\nicefrac{{\pi_{\texttt{base}}}}{{\pi}};\beta})$. We can bound

\displaystyle\En\left[X^{4}\right] \displaystyle=\En\left[\int_{0}^{\infty}\mathbb{I}\left\{X^{4}>t\right\}dt\right] \displaystyle=4\En\left[\int_{0}^{\infty}\mathbb{I}\left\{X>t\right\}t^{3}dt\right] \displaystyle=4\int_{0}^{\infty}\mathbb{P}\left[X>t\right]t^{3}dt \displaystyle\leq{}k^{4}+4\int_{k}^{\infty}\mathbb{P}\left[X>t\right]t^{3}dt \displaystyle\leq{}k^{4}+4\int_{k}^{\infty}e^{k-t}t^{3}dt \displaystyle=k^{4}+4(k^{3}+3k^{2}+6k+6) \displaystyle=O(k^{4}+1),
where the third-to-last line uses Section J.1.1. ∎

sections.text:
The following result is a generalization of Section 4.2.1.

For all $\gamma\in(0,1)$, the model $\pi^{\star}_{\beta}$ satisfies $\mathcal{C}_{\pi^{\star}_{\beta}}\leq(1-\gamma)^{-1}C_{\texttt{cov},\gamma}$ and $\mathcal{C}_{\nicefrac{{\pi_{\texttt{base}}}}{{\pi^{\star}_{\beta}}};\beta}\leq{}\left\lvert\mathcal{Y}\right\rvert$.

Proof of Section J.1.1. For any fixed $x\in\mathcal{X}$, we have

\displaystyle\En_{y\sim\pi^{\star}_{\beta}(\cdot\mid x)}\left[\frac{\pi^{\star}_{\beta}(y\mid x)}{\pi_{\texttt{base}}(y\mid x)}\right] \displaystyle=\En_{y\sim\pi^{\star}_{\beta}(\cdot\mid x)}\left[\frac{\pi_{\texttt{base}}^{1+\beta^{-1}}(y\mid{}x)}{\pi_{\texttt{base}}(y\mid{}x)}\right]\cdot{}\left(\sum_{y^{\prime}\in\mathcal{Y}}\pi_{\texttt{base}}^{1+\beta^{-1}}(y^{\prime}\mid{}x)\right)^{-1} \displaystyle\leq{}\max_{y\in\mathcal{Y}}\pi_{\texttt{base}}^{\beta^{-1}}(y\mid{}x)\cdot{}\left(\sum_{y^{\prime}\in\mathcal{Y}}\pi_{\texttt{base}}^{1+\beta^{-1}}(y^{\prime}\mid{}x)\right)^{-1} \displaystyle\leq{}(1-\gamma)^{-1}\pi_{\texttt{base}}^{\beta^{-1}}(\bm{y}^{\star}_{\gamma}(x)\mid{}x)\cdot{}\left(\sum_{y^{\prime}\in\mathcal{Y}}\pi_{\texttt{base}}^{1+\beta^{-1}}(y^{\prime}\mid{}x)\right)^{-1} \displaystyle=(1-\gamma)^{-1}\frac{\pi_{\texttt{base}}^{1+\beta^{-1}}(\bm{y}^{\star}_{\gamma}(x)\mid{}x)}{\pi_{\texttt{base}}(\bm{y}^{\star}_{\gamma}(x)\mid{}x)}\cdot{}\left(\sum_{y^{\prime}\in\mathcal{Y}}\pi_{\texttt{base}}^{1+\beta^{-1}}(y^{\prime}\mid{}x)\right)^{-1} \displaystyle=(1-\gamma)^{-1}\frac{\sum_{y\in\bm{y}^{\star}_{\gamma}(x)}\pi_{\texttt{base}}^{1+\beta^{-1}}(y\mid{}x)}{\pi_{\texttt{base}}(\bm{y}^{\star}_{\gamma}(x)\mid{}x)}\cdot{}\left(\sum_{y^{\prime}\in\mathcal{Y}}\pi_{\texttt{base}}^{1+\beta^{-1}}(y^{\prime}\mid{}x)\right)^{-1} \displaystyle\leq(1-\gamma)^{-1}\frac{1}{\pi_{\texttt{base}}(\bm{y}^{\star}_{\gamma}(x)\mid{}x)}.

It follows that $\mathcal{C}_{\pi^{\star}_{\beta}}\leq(1-\gamma)^{-1}C_{\texttt{cov},\gamma}$ as claimed.

For the second result, we have

\displaystyle\mathcal{C}_{\nicefrac{{\pi_{\texttt{base}}}}{{\pi^{\star}_{\beta}}};\beta}=\En_{\pi_{\texttt{base}}}\left[\frac{1}{\pi_{\texttt{base}}(y\mid{}x)}\cdot\left(\sum_{y^{\prime}\in\mathcal{Y}}\pi_{\texttt{base}}^{1+\beta^{-1}}(y^{\prime}\mid{}x)\right)^{\beta}\right]\leq{}\En_{\pi_{\texttt{base}}}\left[\frac{1}{\pi_{\texttt{base}}(y\mid{}x)}\right]=\lvert\mathcal{Y}\rvert.

∎

The next lemmas provide bounds on the tails of the self-rewards used in the algorithm.

Suppose $\beta\in[0,1]$. For any model $\pi$, with probability at least $1-\delta$ over the draw of $x\sim\mu$, $y,y^{\prime}\sim\pi_{\texttt{base}}(\cdot\mid x)$, we have that for all $s>0$,

\displaystyle\mathbb{P}\left[\left\lvert\beta\log\left(\frac{\pi(y\mid{}x)}{\pi_{\texttt{base}}(y\mid{}x)}\right)-\beta\log\left(\frac{\pi(y^{\prime}\mid{}x)}{\pi_{\texttt{base}}(y^{\prime}\mid{}x)}\right)\right\rvert>\log(2\mathcal{C}_{\nicefrac{{\pi_{\texttt{base}}}}{{\pi}};\beta})+s\right]\leq\exp\left(-s\right).

Proof of Section J.1.1. Define

X\vcentcolon=\left\lvert\beta\log\left(\frac{\pi(y\mid{}x)}{\pi_{\texttt{base}}(y\mid{}x)}\right)-\beta\log\left(\frac{\pi(y^{\prime}\mid{}x)}{\pi_{\texttt{base}}(y^{\prime}\mid{}x)}\right)\right\rvert.

By the Chernoff method, we have that with probability at least $1-\delta$,

\displaystyle X \displaystyle\leq{}\log(\En\left[\exp(X)\right])+\log(\delta^{-1}) \displaystyle=\log\left(\En_{x\sim\mu,y,y^{\prime}\sim\pi_{\texttt{base}}(x)}\left[\exp\left(\left\lvert\beta\log\left(\frac{\pi(y\mid{}x)}{\pi_{\texttt{base}}(y\mid{}x)}\right)-\beta\log\left(\frac{\pi(y^{\prime}\mid{}x)}{\pi_{\texttt{base}}(y^{\prime}\mid{}x)}\right)\right\rvert\right)\right]\right)+\log(\delta^{-1}) \displaystyle\leq{}\log\Bigg(\En_{x\sim\mu,y,y^{\prime}\sim\pi_{\texttt{base}}(x)}\left[\exp\left(\beta\log\left(\frac{\pi(y\mid{}x)}{\pi_{\texttt{base}}(y\mid{}x)}\right)-\beta\log\left(\frac{\pi(y^{\prime}\mid{}x)}{\pi_{\texttt{base}}(y^{\prime}\mid{}x)}\right)\right)\right] \displaystyle\qquad+\En_{x\sim\mu,y,y^{\prime}\sim\pi_{\texttt{base}}(x)}\left[\exp\left(\beta\log\left(\frac{\pi(y^{\prime}\mid{}x)}{\pi_{\texttt{base}}(y^{\prime}\mid{}x)}\right)-\beta\log\left(\frac{\pi(y\mid{}x)}{\pi_{\texttt{base}}(y\mid{}x)}\right)\right)\right]\Bigg)+\log(\delta^{-1}) \displaystyle=\log\left(2\En_{x\sim\mu,y,y^{\prime}\sim\pi_{\texttt{base}}(x)}\left[\exp\left(\beta\log\left(\frac{\pi(y\mid{}x)}{\pi_{\texttt{base}}(y\mid{}x)}\right)-\beta\log\left(\frac{\pi(y^{\prime}\mid{}x)}{\pi_{\texttt{base}}(y^{\prime}\mid{}x)}\right)\right)\right]\right)+\log(\delta^{-1}) \displaystyle=\log\left(\En_{x\sim\mu,y,y^{\prime}\sim\pi_{\texttt{base}}(x)}\left[\left(\frac{\pi(y\mid{}x)}{\pi_{\texttt{base}}(y\mid{}x)}\cdot\frac{\pi_{\texttt{base}}(y^{\prime}\mid{}x)}{\pi(y^{\prime}\mid{}x)}\right)^{\beta}\right]\right)+\log(2\delta^{-1}).

As long as $\beta\leq{}1$, by Jensen’s inequality, we can bound

\displaystyle\En_{x\sim\mu,y,y^{\prime}\sim\pi_{\texttt{base}}(x)}\left[\left(\frac{\pi(y\mid{}x)}{\pi_{\texttt{base}}(y\mid{}x)}\cdot\frac{\pi_{\texttt{base}}(y^{\prime}\mid{}x)}{\pi(y^{\prime}\mid{}x)}\right)^{\beta}\right] \displaystyle\leq{}\En_{x\sim\mu,y^{\prime}\sim\pi_{\texttt{base}}(x)}\left[\left(\En_{y\sim\pi_{\texttt{base}}(x)}\left[\frac{\pi(y\mid{}x)}{\pi_{\texttt{base}}(y\mid{}x)}\right]\cdot\frac{\pi_{\texttt{base}}(y^{\prime}\mid{}x)}{\pi(y^{\prime}\mid{}x)}\right)^{\beta}\right] \displaystyle=\En_{x\sim\mu,y^{\prime}\sim\pi_{\texttt{base}}(x)}\left[\left(\frac{\pi_{\texttt{base}}(y^{\prime}\mid{}x)}{\pi(y^{\prime}\mid{}x)}\right)^{\beta}\right] \displaystyle=\mathcal{C}_{\nicefrac{{\pi_{\texttt{base}}}}{{\pi}};\beta},

which proves the result. ∎

Let $\beta\in[0,1]$. For all models $\pi$, we have

\displaystyle\En_{x\sim\mu,y,y^{\prime}\sim\pi_{\texttt{base}}(\cdot\mid x)}\left[\left\lvert\beta\log\left(\frac{\pi(y\mid{}x)}{\pi_{\texttt{base}}(y\mid{}x)}\right)-\beta\log\left(\frac{\pi(y^{\prime}\mid{}x)}{\pi_{\texttt{base}}(y^{\prime}\mid{}x)}\right)\right\rvert^{4}\right]\leq{}O(\log^{4}(\mathcal{C}_{\nicefrac{{\pi_{\texttt{base}}}}{{\pi}};\beta})+1).

Proof of Section J.1.1. Define

X\vcentcolon=\left\lvert\beta\log\left(\frac{\pi(y\mid{}x)}{\pi_{\texttt{base}}(y\mid{}x)}\right)-\beta\log\left(\frac{\pi(y^{\prime}\mid{}x)}{\pi_{\texttt{base}}(y^{\prime}\mid{}x)}\right)\right\rvert.

Set $k=\log(2\mathcal{C}_{\nicefrac{{\pi_{\texttt{base}}}}{{\pi}};\beta})$. We can bound

\displaystyle\En\left[X^{4}\right] \displaystyle=\En\left[\int_{0}^{\infty}\mathbb{I}\left\{X^{4}>t\right\}dt\right] \displaystyle=4\En\left[\int_{0}^{\infty}\mathbb{I}\left\{X>t\right\}t^{3}dt\right] \displaystyle=4\int_{0}^{\infty}\mathbb{P}\left[X>t\right]t^{3}dt \displaystyle\leq{}k^{4}+4\int_{k}^{\infty}\mathbb{P}\left[X>t\right]t^{3}dt \displaystyle\leq{}k^{4}+4\int_{k}^{\infty}e^{k-t}t^{3}dt \displaystyle=k^{4}+4(k^{3}+3k^{2}+6k+6) \displaystyle=O(k^{4}+1),

where the third-to-last line uses Section J.1.1. ∎

sections.title: J.1.2 Proof of Section J.1

paragraphs.text: Proof of Section J.1. For any model $\pi\in\Pi$, define $J(\pi)\vcentcolon={}\En_{\pi}\left[\log\pi_{\texttt{base}}(y\mid{}x)\right]$. Let $\widehat{\pi}\in\Pi$ denote the model returned by the DPO algorithm in Eq. 21. Let $\En_{\pi,\pi^{\prime}}\left[\cdot\right]$ denote shorthand for $\En_{x\sim\mu,y\sim\pi(x),y^{\prime}\sim\pi^{\prime}(x)}[\cdot]$, and for any $r:\mathcal{X}\times\mathcal{Y}\to\mathbb{R}$ define $\Delta^{r}(x,y,y^{\prime}):=r(x,y)-r(x,y^{\prime})$. Define
r^{\star}(x,y):=\log\pi_{\texttt{base}}(y\mid{}x)=\beta\log\left(\frac{\pi^{\star}_{\beta}(y\mid{}x)}{\pi_{\texttt{base}}(y\mid{}x)}\right)+Z(x),
and let $\widehat{r}(x,y)\vcentcolon={}\beta\log\left(\frac{\widehat{\pi}(y\mid{}x)}{\pi_{\texttt{base}}(y\mid{}x)}\right)$. By a standard argument (Huang et al., 2024), we have
\displaystyle\widehat{\pi}\in\argmax_{\pi:\mathcal{X}\to\Delta(\mathcal{Y})}\En_{\pi}[\widehat{r}(x,y)]-\beta D_{\mathsf{KL}}\left(\pi\,\|\,\pi_{\texttt{base}}\right).
Therefore for any comparator model $\pi^{\star}:\mathcal{X}\to\Delta(\mathcal{Y})$ (not necessarily in the model class $\Pi$), we have

\displaystyle J(\pi^{\star})-J(\widehat{\pi}) \displaystyle=\En_{\pi^{\star}}[r^{\star}(x,y)]-\En_{\widehat{\pi}}[r^{\star}(x,y)] \displaystyle=\En_{\pi^{\star}}[\widehat{r}(x,y)]-\beta D_{\mathsf{KL}}\left(\pi^{\star}\,\|\,\pi_{\texttt{base}}\right)-\En_{\widehat{\pi}}[\widehat{r}(x,y)]+\beta D_{\mathsf{KL}}\left(\widehat{\pi}\,\|\,\pi_{\texttt{base}}\right) \displaystyle\qquad+\En_{\pi^{\star}}[r^{\star}(x,y)-\widehat{r}(x,y)]+\beta D_{\mathsf{KL}}\left(\pi^{\star}\,\|\,\pi_{\texttt{base}}\right)+\En_{\widehat{\pi}}[\widehat{r}(x,y)-r^{\star}(x,y)]-\beta D_{\mathsf{KL}}\left(\widehat{\pi}\,\|\,\pi_{\texttt{base}}\right) \displaystyle\leq\En_{\pi^{\star}}[r^{\star}(x,y)-\widehat{r}(x,y)]+\beta D_{\mathsf{KL}}\left(\pi^{\star}\,\|\,\pi_{\texttt{base}}\right)+\En_{\widehat{\pi}}[\widehat{r}(x,y)-r^{\star}(x,y)]-\beta D_{\mathsf{KL}}\left(\widehat{\pi}\,\|\,\pi_{\texttt{base}}\right) \displaystyle=\En_{\pi^{\star},\pi_{\texttt{base}}}\left[\Delta^{r^{\star}}(x,y,y^{\prime})-\Delta^{\widehat{r}}(x,y,y^{\prime})\right]+\En_{\widehat{\pi},\pi_{\texttt{base}}}\left[\Delta^{\widehat{r}}(x,y,y^{\prime})-\Delta^{r^{\star}}(x,y,y^{\prime})\right] \displaystyle\qquad+\beta D_{\mathsf{KL}}\left(\pi^{\star}\,\|\,\pi_{\texttt{base}}\right)-\beta D_{\mathsf{KL}}\left(\widehat{\pi}\,\|\,\pi_{\texttt{base}}\right)
where the inequality uses Eq. 165. To bound the right-hand side above, we will use the following lemma, which is proven in the sequel. For any model $\pi$ and any $\eta>0$, we have that

\displaystyle\En_{\pi,\pi_{\texttt{base}}}\left[\left\lvert\Delta^{r^{\star}}(x,y,y^{\prime})-\Delta^{\widehat{r}}(x,y,y^{\prime})\right\rvert\right] \displaystyle\lesssim{}\mathcal{C}_{\pi}^{1/2}\cdot\left(\En_{\pi_{\texttt{base}},\pi_{\texttt{base}}}\left[\left\lvert\Delta^{r^{\star}}(x,y,y^{\prime})-\Delta^{\widehat{r}}(x,y,y^{\prime})\right\rvert^{2}\mathbb{I}\left\{\big\lvert\Delta^{r^{\star}}\big\rvert\leq\eta,\big\lvert\Delta^{\widehat{r}}\big\rvert\leq\eta\right\}\right]\right)^{1/2} \displaystyle~~~~+\mathcal{C}_{\pi}^{1/2}(\log(\mathcal{C}_{\nicefrac{{\pi_{\texttt{base}}}}{{\widehat{\pi}}};\beta})+\log(\mathcal{C}_{\nicefrac{{\pi_{\texttt{base}}}}{{\pi^{\star}_{\beta}}};\beta}))\cdot\left(\mathbb{P}_{\pi_{\texttt{base}},\pi_{\texttt{base}}}\left[\big\lvert\Delta^{r^{\star}}\big\rvert>\eta\right]+\mathbb{P}_{\pi_{\texttt{base}},\pi_{\texttt{base}}}\left[\big\lvert\Delta^{\widehat{r}}\big\rvert>\eta\right]\right)^{1/4}.

Using Section J.1.2 to bound the first two terms of Eq. 171, and using the fact that all $\pi\in\Pi$ have $\mathcal{C}_{\pi}\leq C_{\texttt{conc}}$ and $\mathcal{C}_{\nicefrac{{\pi_{\texttt{base}}}}{{\pi}};\beta}\leq C_{\texttt{loss}}$, we have that

\displaystyle J(\pi^{\star})-J(\widehat{\pi}) \displaystyle\lesssim{}(\mathcal{C}_{\pi^{\star}}+C_{\texttt{conc}})^{1/2}\cdot\left(\En_{\pi_{\texttt{base}},\pi_{\texttt{base}}}\left[\left\lvert\Delta^{r^{\star}}(x,y,y^{\prime})-\Delta^{\widehat{r}}(x,y,y^{\prime})\right\rvert^{2}\mathbb{I}\left\{\big\lvert\Delta^{r^{\star}}\big\rvert\leq\eta,\big\lvert\Delta^{\widehat{r}}\big\rvert\leq\eta\right\}\right]\right)^{1/2} \displaystyle+(\mathcal{C}_{\pi^{\star}}+C_{\texttt{conc}})^{1/2}\log(C_{\texttt{loss}})\cdot\left(\mathbb{P}_{\pi_{\texttt{base}},\pi_{\texttt{base}}}\left[\big\lvert\Delta^{r^{\star}}\big\rvert>\eta\right]+\mathbb{P}_{\pi_{\texttt{base}},\pi_{\texttt{base}}}\left[\big\lvert\Delta^{\widehat{r}}\big\rvert>\eta\right]\right)^{1/4}+\beta D_{\mathsf{KL}}\left(\pi^{\star}\,\|\,\pi_{\texttt{base}}\right).

Let us overload notation and write $\Delta^{\pi}(x,y,y^{\prime})=\beta\log\left(\frac{\pi(y\mid{}x)}{\pi_{\texttt{base}}(y\mid{}x)}\right)-\beta\log\left(\frac{\pi(y^{\prime}\mid{}x)}{\pi_{\texttt{base}}(y^{\prime}\mid{}x)}\right)$, so that $\Delta^{\widehat{\pi}}=\Delta^{\widehat{r}}$ and $\Delta^{\pi^{\star}_{\beta}}=\Delta^{r^{\star}}$. Since $\pi^{\star}_{\beta}\in\Pi$, the definition of $\widehat{\pi}$ in Eq. 7 implies that

\displaystyle\sum_{(x,y,y^{\prime})\in\mathcal{D}_{\texttt{pref}}}\left(\Delta^{\widehat{\pi}}(x,y,y^{\prime})-\Delta^{\pi^{\star}_{\beta}}(x,y,y^{\prime})\right)^{2} \displaystyle\leq{}\min_{\pi\in\Pi}\sum_{(x,y,y^{\prime})\in\mathcal{D}_{\texttt{pref}}}\left(\Delta^{\pi}(x,y,y^{\prime})-\Delta^{\pi^{\star}_{\beta}}(x,y,y^{\prime})\right)^{2} \displaystyle\leq{}\sum_{(x,y,y^{\prime})\in\mathcal{D}_{\texttt{pref}}}\left(\Delta^{\pi^{\star}_{\beta}}(x,y,y^{\prime})-\Delta^{\pi^{\star}_{\beta}}(x,y,y^{\prime})\right)^{2} \displaystyle=0.
Define $B_{n,\rho}:=\log(2nC_{\texttt{loss}}\lvert\Pi\rvert\rho^{-1})$. It is immediate that

\displaystyle\sum_{(x,y,y^{\prime})\in\mathcal{D}_{\texttt{pref}}}\left(\Delta^{\widehat{\pi}}(x,y,y^{\prime})-\Delta^{\pi^{\star}_{\beta}}(x,y,y^{\prime})\right)^{2}\mathbb{I}\left\{\big\lvert\Delta^{\widehat{\pi}}\big\rvert\leq B_{n,\rho},\big\lvert\Delta^{\pi^{\star}_{\beta}}\big\rvert\leq B_{n,\rho}\right\}\leq{}0.
From here, Bernstein’s inequality and a union bound implies that with probability at least $1-\rho$,

\displaystyle\En_{\pi_{\texttt{base}},\pi_{\texttt{base}}}\left[\left\lvert\Delta^{\widehat{\pi}}(x,y,y^{\prime})-\Delta^{\pi^{\star}_{\beta}}(x,y,y^{\prime})\right\rvert^{2}\mathbb{I}\left\{\big\lvert\Delta^{\widehat{\pi}}\big\rvert\leq B_{n,\rho},\big\lvert\Delta^{\pi^{\star}_{\beta}}\big\rvert\leq B_{n,\rho}\right\}\right] \displaystyle\lesssim{}\frac{B_{n,\rho}^{2}\log(\lvert\Pi\rvert\rho^{-1})}{n}=\vcentcolon\varepsilon_{\texttt{stat}}^{2}.
In particular, if we combine this with Eq. 177 and set $\eta=B_{n,\rho}$, then Section J.1.1 implies that

\displaystyle J(\pi^{\star})-J(\widehat{\pi}) \displaystyle\lesssim{}(\mathcal{C}_{\pi^{\star}}+C_{\texttt{conc}})^{1/2}\cdot\varepsilon_{\texttt{stat}}+(\mathcal{C}_{\pi^{\star}}+C_{\texttt{conc}})^{1/2}\log(C_{\texttt{loss}})\cdot\rho^{1/4}+\beta D_{\mathsf{KL}}\left(\pi^{\star}\,\|\,\pi_{\texttt{base}}\right).
Note that the above bound holds for any $\pi^{\star}:\mathcal{X}\to\Delta(\mathcal{Y})$. We define $\pi^{\star}$ by
\pi^{\star}(y\mid x):=\frac{\pi_{\texttt{base}}(y\mid x)\mathbb{I}[y\in\bm{y}^{\star}_{\gamma}(x)]}{\pi_{\texttt{base}}(\bm{y}^{\star}_{\gamma}(x)\mid x)},

which can be seen to satisfy $\mathcal{C}_{\pi^{\star}}\leq{}C_{\texttt{cov},\gamma}\leq C_{\texttt{conc}}$ and $D_{\mathsf{KL}}\left(\pi^{\star}\,\|\,\pi_{\texttt{base}}\right)\leq\log(\mathcal{C}_{\pi^{\star}})\leq\log(C_{\texttt{conc}})$. With this choice, we can further bound the expression above by

\displaystyle J(\pi^{\star})-J(\widehat{\pi}) \displaystyle\lesssim{}(C_{\texttt{conc}})^{1/2}\cdot\varepsilon_{\texttt{stat}}+(C_{\texttt{conc}})^{1/2}\log(C_{\texttt{loss}})\cdot\rho^{1/4}+\beta\log(C_{\texttt{conc}})
Given a desired failure probability $\rho$, applying the bound above with $\rho^{\prime}\vcentcolon={}\rho\wedge{}(\varepsilon_{\texttt{stat}}/\log(C_{\texttt{loss}}))^{4}$ then gives
\displaystyle J(\pi^{\star})-J(\widehat{\pi}) \displaystyle\lesssim{}(C_{\texttt{conc}})^{1/2}\cdot\varepsilon_{\texttt{stat}}+\beta\log(C_{\texttt{conc}}).
Finally, we observe that for our choice of $\pi^{\star}$, under the margin condition with parameter $\gamma$, we have

\displaystyle J(\pi^{\star})-J(\widehat{\pi}) \displaystyle=\En_{x\sim\mu}\En_{y,y^{\prime}\sim\pi^{\star},\widehat{\pi}}\left[\log\left(\frac{\pi_{\texttt{base}}(y\mid{}x)}{\pi_{\texttt{base}}(y^{\prime}\mid{}x)}\right)\right] \displaystyle\gtrsim{}\gamma_{\mathsf{margin}}\cdot\En_{x\sim\mu}\En_{y^{\prime}\sim\widehat{\pi}}\left[\mathbb{I}\{y^{\prime}\not\in\bm{y}^{\star}_{\gamma}(x)\}\right]-\gamma \displaystyle\gtrsim{}\gamma_{\mathsf{margin}}\delta\cdot\En_{x\sim\mu}\left[\mathbb{I}\{\widehat{\pi}(\bm{y}^{\star}_{\gamma}(x)\mid{}x)\leq{}1-\delta\}\right]-\gamma

where the first inequality uses Section J.1 together with the fact that $y\in\bm{y}^{\star}_{\gamma}(x)$ with probability $1$ over $x\sim\mu$ and $y\sim\pi^{\star}(\cdot\mid x)$. This proves the result.
Proof of Section J.1.2. For any $\eta>0$, we can bound

\displaystyle\En_{\pi,\pi_{\texttt{base}}}\left[\left\lvert\Delta^{r^{\star}}(x,y,y^{\prime})-\Delta^{\widehat{r}}(x,y,y^{\prime})\right\rvert\right] \displaystyle\leq{}\En_{\pi,\pi_{\texttt{base}}}\left[\left\lvert\Delta^{r^{\star}}(x,y,y^{\prime})-\Delta^{\widehat{r}}(x,y,y^{\prime})\right\rvert\mathbb{I}\left\{\big\lvert\Delta^{r^{\star}}\big\rvert\leq\eta,\big\lvert\Delta^{\widehat{r}}\big\rvert\leq\eta\right\}\right] \displaystyle~~~~+\En_{\pi,\pi_{\texttt{base}}}\left[\left\lvert\Delta^{r^{\star}}(x,y,y^{\prime})-\Delta^{\widehat{r}}(x,y,y^{\prime})\right\rvert\mathbb{I}\left\{\big\lvert\Delta^{r^{\star}}\big\rvert>\eta\vee\big\lvert\Delta^{\widehat{r}}\big\rvert>\eta\right\}\right].
For the second term above, we can use Cauchy-Schwarz to bound

\displaystyle\En_{\pi,\pi_{\texttt{base}}}\left[\left\lvert\Delta^{r^{\star}}(x,y,y^{\prime})-\Delta^{\widehat{r}}(x,y,y^{\prime})\right\rvert\mathbb{I}\left\{\big\lvert\Delta^{r^{\star}}\big\rvert>\eta\vee\big\lvert\Delta^{\widehat{r}}\big\rvert>\eta\right\}\right] \displaystyle\leq{}\mathcal{C}_{\pi}^{1/2}\cdot\left(\En_{\pi_{\texttt{base}},\pi_{\texttt{base}}}\left[\left\lvert\Delta^{r^{\star}}(x,y,y^{\prime})-\Delta^{\widehat{r}}(x,y,y^{\prime})\right\rvert^{2}\mathbb{I}\left\{\big\lvert\Delta^{r^{\star}}\big\rvert>\eta\vee\big\lvert\Delta^{\widehat{r}}\big\rvert>\eta\right\}\right]\right)^{1/2} \displaystyle\lesssim{}\mathcal{C}_{\pi}^{1/2}\cdot\left(\mathbb{P}_{\pi_{\texttt{base}},\pi_{\texttt{base}}}\left[\big\lvert\Delta^{r^{\star}}\big\rvert>\eta\right]+\mathbb{P}_{\pi_{\texttt{base}},\pi_{\texttt{base}}}\left[\big\lvert\Delta^{\widehat{r}}\big\rvert>\eta\right]\right)^{1/4} \displaystyle\qquad\qquad\cdot{}\left(\En_{\pi_{\texttt{base}},\pi_{\texttt{base}}}\left[\left\lvert\Delta^{r^{\star}}(x,y,y^{\prime})\right\rvert^{4}\right]+\En_{\pi_{\texttt{base}},\pi_{\texttt{base}}}\left[\left\lvert\Delta^{\widehat{r}}(x,y,y^{\prime})\right\rvert^{4}\right]\right)^{1/4} \displaystyle\lesssim{}\mathcal{C}_{\pi}^{1/2}\cdot\left(\mathbb{P}_{\pi_{\texttt{base}},\pi_{\texttt{base}}}\left[\big\lvert\Delta^{r^{\star}}\big\rvert>\eta\right]+\mathbb{P}_{\pi_{\texttt{base}},\pi_{\texttt{base}}}\left[\big\lvert\Delta^{\widehat{r}}\big\rvert>\eta\right]\right)^{1/4}\cdot{}(\log(\mathcal{C}_{\nicefrac{{\pi_{\texttt{base}}}}{{\widehat{\pi}}};\beta})+\log(\mathcal{C}_{\nicefrac{{\pi_{\texttt{base}}}}{{\pi^{\star}_{\beta}}};\beta})),
where the last inequality follows from Section J.1.1.
Meanwhile, for the first term, for any $\lambda>0$ we can bound

\displaystyle\En_{\pi,\pi_{\texttt{base}}}\left[\left\lvert\Delta^{r^{\star}}(x,y,y^{\prime})-\Delta^{\widehat{r}}(x,y,y^{\prime})\right\rvert\mathbb{I}\left\{\big\lvert\Delta^{r^{\star}}\big\rvert\leq\eta,\big\lvert\Delta^{\widehat{r}}\big\rvert\leq\eta\right\}\right] \displaystyle\leq{}\mathcal{C}_{\pi}^{1/2}\left(\En_{\pi_{\texttt{base}},\pi_{\texttt{base}}}\left[\left\lvert\Delta^{r^{\star}}(x,y,y^{\prime})-\Delta^{\widehat{r}}(x,y,y^{\prime})\right\rvert^{2}\mathbb{I}\left\{\big\lvert\Delta^{r^{\star}}\big\rvert\leq\eta,\big\lvert\Delta^{\widehat{r}}\big\rvert\leq\eta\right\}\right]\right)^{1/2}.

Define $B_{n,\rho}:=\log(2nC_{\texttt{loss}}\lvert\Pi\rvert\rho^{-1})$. It is immediate that

\displaystyle\sum_{(x,y,y^{\prime})\in\mathcal{D}_{\texttt{pref}}}\left(\Delta^{\widehat{\pi}}(x,y,y^{\prime})-\Delta^{\pi^{\star}_{\beta}}(x,y,y^{\prime})\right)^{2}\mathbb{I}\left\{\big\lvert\Delta^{\widehat{\pi}}\big\rvert\leq B_{n,\rho},\big\lvert\Delta^{\pi^{\star}_{\beta}}\big\rvert\leq B_{n,\rho}\right\}\leq{}0.

\displaystyle\En_{\pi_{\texttt{base}},\pi_{\texttt{base}}}\left[\left\lvert\Delta^{\widehat{\pi}}(x,y,y^{\prime})-\Delta^{\pi^{\star}_{\beta}}(x,y,y^{\prime})\right\rvert^{2}\mathbb{I}\left\{\big\lvert\Delta^{\widehat{\pi}}\big\rvert\leq B_{n,\rho},\big\lvert\Delta^{\pi^{\star}_{\beta}}\big\rvert\leq B_{n,\rho}\right\}\right] \displaystyle\lesssim{}\frac{B_{n,\rho}^{2}\log(\lvert\Pi\rvert\rho^{-1})}{n}=\vcentcolon\varepsilon_{\texttt{stat}}^{2}.

\displaystyle J(\pi^{\star})-J(\widehat{\pi}) \displaystyle\lesssim{}(\mathcal{C}_{\pi^{\star}}+C_{\texttt{conc}})^{1/2}\cdot\varepsilon_{\texttt{stat}}+(\mathcal{C}_{\pi^{\star}}+C_{\texttt{conc}})^{1/2}\log(C_{\texttt{loss}})\cdot\rho^{1/4}+\beta D_{\mathsf{KL}}\left(\pi^{\star}\,\|\,\pi_{\texttt{base}}\right).

Note that the above bound holds for any $\pi^{\star}:\mathcal{X}\to\Delta(\mathcal{Y})$. We define $\pi^{\star}$ by

\pi^{\star}(y\mid x):=\frac{\pi_{\texttt{base}}(y\mid x)\mathbb{I}[y\in\bm{y}^{\star}_{\gamma}(x)]}{\pi_{\texttt{base}}(\bm{y}^{\star}_{\gamma}(x)\mid x)},

which can be seen to satisfy $\mathcal{C}_{\pi^{\star}}\leq{}C_{\texttt{cov},\gamma}\leq C_{\texttt{conc}}$ and $D_{\mathsf{KL}}\left(\pi^{\star}\,\|\,\pi_{\texttt{base}}\right)\leq\log(\mathcal{C}_{\pi^{\star}})\leq\log(C_{\texttt{conc}})$. With this choice, we can further bound the expression above by

\displaystyle J(\pi^{\star})-J(\widehat{\pi}) \displaystyle\lesssim{}(C_{\texttt{conc}})^{1/2}\cdot\varepsilon_{\texttt{stat}}+(C_{\texttt{conc}})^{1/2}\log(C_{\texttt{loss}})\cdot\rho^{1/4}+\beta\log(C_{\texttt{conc}})

Given a desired failure probability $\rho$, applying the bound above with $\rho^{\prime}\vcentcolon={}\rho\wedge{}(\varepsilon_{\texttt{stat}}/\log(C_{\texttt{loss}}))^{4}$ then gives

\displaystyle J(\pi^{\star})-J(\widehat{\pi}) \displaystyle\lesssim{}(C_{\texttt{conc}})^{1/2}\cdot\varepsilon_{\texttt{stat}}+\beta\log(C_{\texttt{conc}}).

Finally, we observe that for our choice of $\pi^{\star}$, under the margin condition with parameter $\gamma$, we have

\displaystyle J(\pi^{\star})-J(\widehat{\pi}) \displaystyle=\En_{x\sim\mu}\En_{y,y^{\prime}\sim\pi^{\star},\widehat{\pi}}\left[\log\left(\frac{\pi_{\texttt{base}}(y\mid{}x)}{\pi_{\texttt{base}}(y^{\prime}\mid{}x)}\right)\right] \displaystyle\gtrsim{}\gamma_{\mathsf{margin}}\cdot\En_{x\sim\mu}\En_{y^{\prime}\sim\widehat{\pi}}\left[\mathbb{I}\{y^{\prime}\not\in\bm{y}^{\star}_{\gamma}(x)\}\right]-\gamma \displaystyle\gtrsim{}\gamma_{\mathsf{margin}}\delta\cdot\En_{x\sim\mu}\left[\mathbb{I}\{\widehat{\pi}(\bm{y}^{\star}_{\gamma}(x)\mid{}x)\leq{}1-\delta\}\right]-\gamma

where the first inequality uses Section J.1 together with the fact that $y\in\bm{y}^{\star}_{\gamma}(x)$ with probability $1$ over $x\sim\mu$ and $y\sim\pi^{\star}(\cdot\mid x)$. This proves the result.

∎

Proof of Section J.1.2. For any $\eta>0$, we can bound

\displaystyle\En_{\pi,\pi_{\texttt{base}}}\left[\left\lvert\Delta^{r^{\star}}(x,y,y^{\prime})-\Delta^{\widehat{r}}(x,y,y^{\prime})\right\rvert\right] \displaystyle\leq{}\En_{\pi,\pi_{\texttt{base}}}\left[\left\lvert\Delta^{r^{\star}}(x,y,y^{\prime})-\Delta^{\widehat{r}}(x,y,y^{\prime})\right\rvert\mathbb{I}\left\{\big\lvert\Delta^{r^{\star}}\big\rvert\leq\eta,\big\lvert\Delta^{\widehat{r}}\big\rvert\leq\eta\right\}\right] \displaystyle~~~~+\En_{\pi,\pi_{\texttt{base}}}\left[\left\lvert\Delta^{r^{\star}}(x,y,y^{\prime})-\Delta^{\widehat{r}}(x,y,y^{\prime})\right\rvert\mathbb{I}\left\{\big\lvert\Delta^{r^{\star}}\big\rvert>\eta\vee\big\lvert\Delta^{\widehat{r}}\big\rvert>\eta\right\}\right].

For the second term above, we can use Cauchy-Schwarz to bound

\displaystyle\En_{\pi,\pi_{\texttt{base}}}\left[\left\lvert\Delta^{r^{\star}}(x,y,y^{\prime})-\Delta^{\widehat{r}}(x,y,y^{\prime})\right\rvert\mathbb{I}\left\{\big\lvert\Delta^{r^{\star}}\big\rvert>\eta\vee\big\lvert\Delta^{\widehat{r}}\big\rvert>\eta\right\}\right] \displaystyle\leq{}\mathcal{C}_{\pi}^{1/2}\cdot\left(\En_{\pi_{\texttt{base}},\pi_{\texttt{base}}}\left[\left\lvert\Delta^{r^{\star}}(x,y,y^{\prime})-\Delta^{\widehat{r}}(x,y,y^{\prime})\right\rvert^{2}\mathbb{I}\left\{\big\lvert\Delta^{r^{\star}}\big\rvert>\eta\vee\big\lvert\Delta^{\widehat{r}}\big\rvert>\eta\right\}\right]\right)^{1/2} \displaystyle\lesssim{}\mathcal{C}_{\pi}^{1/2}\cdot\left(\mathbb{P}_{\pi_{\texttt{base}},\pi_{\texttt{base}}}\left[\big\lvert\Delta^{r^{\star}}\big\rvert>\eta\right]+\mathbb{P}_{\pi_{\texttt{base}},\pi_{\texttt{base}}}\left[\big\lvert\Delta^{\widehat{r}}\big\rvert>\eta\right]\right)^{1/4} \displaystyle\qquad\qquad\cdot{}\left(\En_{\pi_{\texttt{base}},\pi_{\texttt{base}}}\left[\left\lvert\Delta^{r^{\star}}(x,y,y^{\prime})\right\rvert^{4}\right]+\En_{\pi_{\texttt{base}},\pi_{\texttt{base}}}\left[\left\lvert\Delta^{\widehat{r}}(x,y,y^{\prime})\right\rvert^{4}\right]\right)^{1/4} \displaystyle\lesssim{}\mathcal{C}_{\pi}^{1/2}\cdot\left(\mathbb{P}_{\pi_{\texttt{base}},\pi_{\texttt{base}}}\left[\big\lvert\Delta^{r^{\star}}\big\rvert>\eta\right]+\mathbb{P}_{\pi_{\texttt{base}},\pi_{\texttt{base}}}\left[\big\lvert\Delta^{\widehat{r}}\big\rvert>\eta\right]\right)^{1/4}\cdot{}(\log(\mathcal{C}_{\nicefrac{{\pi_{\texttt{base}}}}{{\widehat{\pi}}};\beta})+\log(\mathcal{C}_{\nicefrac{{\pi_{\texttt{base}}}}{{\pi^{\star}_{\beta}}};\beta})),

where the last inequality follows from Section J.1.1.

Meanwhile, for the first term, for any $\lambda>0$ we can bound

\displaystyle\En_{\pi,\pi_{\texttt{base}}}\left[\left\lvert\Delta^{r^{\star}}(x,y,y^{\prime})-\Delta^{\widehat{r}}(x,y,y^{\prime})\right\rvert\mathbb{I}\left\{\big\lvert\Delta^{r^{\star}}\big\rvert\leq\eta,\big\lvert\Delta^{\widehat{r}}\big\rvert\leq\eta\right\}\right] \displaystyle\leq{}\mathcal{C}_{\pi}^{1/2}\left(\En_{\pi_{\texttt{base}},\pi_{\texttt{base}}}\left[\left\lvert\Delta^{r^{\star}}(x,y,y^{\prime})-\Delta^{\widehat{r}}(x,y,y^{\prime})\right\rvert^{2}\mathbb{I}\left\{\big\lvert\Delta^{r^{\star}}\big\rvert\leq\eta,\big\lvert\Delta^{\widehat{r}}\big\rvert\leq\eta\right\}\right]\right)^{1/2}.

∎

paragraphs.text: In this section we prove Section 4.2.2 as well as Section 4.2.2, the application to linear softmax models. For the formal theorem statements, see Section J.2.3 and Section J.2.4 respectively. The section is organized as follows.
• Section J.2.1 gives necessary background on KL-regularized policy optimization, as well as the Sequential Extrapolation Coefficient.

• Section J.2.3 instantiates the result above with the self-reward function $r(x,y):=\log\pi_{\texttt{base}}(y\mid x)$ to prove Section 4.2.2.

paragraphs.text: To begin, we give background on KL-regularized policy optimization and the Sequential Extrapolation Coefficient.
KL-regularized policy optimization

Let $\beta>0$ be given, and let $r:\mathcal{X}\times\mathcal{Y}\to[-R_{\mathsf{max}},R_{\mathsf{max}}]$ be an unknown reward function on prompt/action pairs. Define a value function $J_{\beta}$ over model class $\Pi$ by:
\displaystyle J_{\beta}(\pi):=\En_{\pi}[r(x,y)]-\beta\cdot D_{\mathsf{KL}}\left(\mathbb{P}^{\pi}\,\|\,\mathbb{P}^{\pi_{\texttt{base}}}\right).

We refer to this as a KL-regularized policy optimization objective (we use the term “policy” following the reinforcement learning literature; for our setting, policies correspond to models). Given query access to $r$, the goal is to find $\widehat{\pi}\in\Pi$ such that
\displaystyle J_{\beta}(\pi^{\star}_{\beta})-J_{\beta}(\widehat{\pi})\leq\epsilon
where $\pi^{\star}_{\beta}(y\mid x)\propto\pi_{\texttt{base}}(y\mid x)\exp(\beta^{-1}r(x,y))$ is the model that maximizes $J_{\beta}$ over all models $\pi:\mathcal{X}\to\Delta(\mathcal{Y})$.
We make use of the following assumptions, as in Xie et al. (2024).
[Realizability] It holds that $\pi^{\star}_{\beta}\in\Pi$.
[Bounded density ratios] For all $\pi\in\Pi$, $(x,y)\in\mathcal{X}\times\mathcal{Y}$, $\big\lvert\beta\log\frac{\pi(y\mid x)}{\pi_{\texttt{base}}(y\mid x)}\big\rvert\leq V_{\mathsf{max}}$.
Finally, we require two definitions.

[Sequential Extrapolation Coefficient for RLHF, (Xie et al., 2024)] For a model class $\Pi$, reward function $r$, reference model $\pi_{\texttt{base}}$, and parameters $T\in\mathbb{N}$ and $\beta,\lambda>0$, the Sequential Extrapolation Coefficient is defined as

\displaystyle\mathsf{SEC}(\Pi,r,T,\beta,\lambda;\pi_{\texttt{base}}) \displaystyle:=\sup_{\pi^{(1)},\dots,\pi^{(T)}\in\Pi}\left\{\sum_{t=1}^{T}\frac{\mathbb{E}^{(t)}\left[\beta\log\frac{\pi^{(t)}(y\mid x)}{\pi_{\texttt{base}}(y\mid x)}-r(x,y)-\beta\log\frac{\pi^{(t)}(y^{\prime}\mid x)}{\pi_{\texttt{base}}(y^{\prime}\mid x)}+r(x,y^{\prime})\right]^{2}}{\lambda\lor\sum_{i=1}^{t-1}\mathbb{E}^{(i)}\left[\left(\beta\log\frac{\pi^{(t)}(y\mid x)}{\pi_{\texttt{base}}(y\mid x)}-r(x,y)-\beta\log\frac{\pi^{(t)}(y^{\prime}\mid x)}{\pi_{\texttt{base}}(y^{\prime}\mid x)}+r(x,y^{\prime})\right)^{2}\right]}\right\}
where $\mathbb{E}^{(t)}$ denotes expectation over $x\sim\mu$, $y\sim\pi^{(t)}(\cdot\mid x)$, and $y^{\prime}\sim\pi_{\texttt{base}}(\cdot\mid x)$.
Let $\epsilon>0$. We say that $\Psi\subseteq\Pi$ is a $\epsilon$-net for model class $\Pi$ if for every $\pi\in\Pi$ there exists $\pi^{\prime}\in\Psi$ such that
\max_{x\in\mathcal{X}}\max_{y\in\mathcal{Y}}\left|\log\frac{\pi(y\mid x)}{\pi^{\prime}(y\mid x)}\right|\leq\epsilon.
We write $\mathcal{N}(\Pi,\epsilon)$ to denote the size of the smallest $\epsilon$-net for $\Pi$.

sections.title: J.2.2 Guarantees for KL-regularized policy optimization with XPO

J.2.2 Guarantees for KL-regularized policy optimization with XPO

paragraphs.text: Algorithm 1 Reward-based variant of Exploratory Preference Optimization (Xie et al., 2024)

input: Base model $\pi_{\texttt{base}}:\mathcal{X}\to\Delta(\mathcal{Y})$, reward function $r:\mathcal{X}\times\mathcal{Y}\to\mathbb{R}$, number of iterations $T\in\mathbb{N}$, KL regularization coefficient $\beta>0$, optimism coefficient $\alpha>0$.
Initialize: $\pi^{(1)}\leftarrow\pi_{\texttt{base}}$, $\mathcal{D}^{(0)}\leftarrow\varnothing$.
for iteration $t=1,\dots,T$ do
Generate sample: $(x^{(t)},y^{(t)},\widetilde{y}^{(t)})$ via $x^{(t)}\sim\mu$, $y^{(t)}\sim\pi^{(t)}(\cdot\mid x^{(t)})$, $\widetilde{y}^{(t)}\sim\pi_{\texttt{base}}(\cdot\mid x^{(t)})$.
Update dataset: $\mathcal{D}^{(t)}\leftarrow\mathcal{D}^{(t-1)}\cup\{(x^{(t)},y^{(t)},\widetilde{y}^{(t)})\}$.
Model optimization with global optimism: $\displaystyle\pi^{(t+1)}$ $\displaystyle\leftarrow\argmin_{\pi\in\Pi}\Bigg\{\alpha\sum_{(x,y,y^{\prime})\in\mathcal{D}^{(t)}}\log(\pi(y^{\prime}\mid x))$ (205) $\displaystyle-\sum_{(x,y,y^{\prime})\in\mathcal{D}^{(t)}}\left(\beta\log\frac{\pi(y\mid x)}{\pi_{\texttt{base}}(y\mid x)}-\beta\log\frac{\pi(y^{\prime}\mid x)}{\pi_{\texttt{base}}(y^{\prime}\mid x)}-(r(x,y)-r(x,y^{\prime}))\right)^{2}\Bigg\}.$ (206)
return: $\widehat{\pi}\leftarrow\argmax_{t\in[T+1]}J_{\beta}(\pi^{(t)})$. $\triangleright$ Can estimate $J_{\beta}(\pi^{(t)})$ using validation data.

In this section, we give self-contained guarantees for the XPO algorithm (Algorithm 1). XPO was introduced in Xie et al. (2024) for KL-regularized policy optimization in the related setting where the learner only has indirect access to the reward function $r$ through preference data (specifically, pairs of actions labeled via a Bradley-Terry model). Standard offline algorithms for this problem, such as DPO, require bounds on concentrability of the model class (see e.g. Eq. 22). Xie et al. (2024) show that the XPO algorithm avoids this dependence, and instead requires bounded Sequential Extrapolation Coefficient.

Algorithm 1 is a variant of the XPO algorithm which is adapted to reward-based feedback (as opposed to preference-based feedback), and Section J.2.2 shows that this algorithm enjoys guarantees similar to those of Xie et al. (2024) for this setting. Note that this is not an immediate corollary of the results in Xie et al. (2024), since the sample complexity in the preference-based setting scales with $e^{O(R_{\mathsf{max}})}$, and for our application to sharpening it is important to avoid this dependence. However, our algorithm and analysis only diverge from Xie et al. (2024) in a few places.

[Variant of Xie et al. (2024, Theorem 3.1)] Suppose that Sections J.2.1 and J.2.1 hold. For any $T\in\mathbb{N}$, $\epsilon_{\mathsf{disc}},\rho\in(0,1)$, by setting $\alpha:=\frac{\beta}{R_{\mathsf{max}}+V_{\mathsf{max}}}\sqrt{\frac{\log(2\mathcal{N}(\Pi,\epsilon_{\mathsf{disc}})T/\rho)}{\mathsf{SEC}(\Pi)T}}$, Algorithm 1 produces a model $\widehat{\pi}\in\Pi$ such that with probability at least $1-\rho$,

\displaystyle\beta D_{\mathsf{KL}}\left(\widehat{\pi}\,\|\,\pi^{\star}_{\beta}\right)=J_{\beta}(\pi^{\star}_{\beta})-J_{\beta}(\widehat{\pi}) \displaystyle\lesssim(R_{\mathsf{max}}+V_{\mathsf{max}})\sqrt{\frac{\mathsf{SEC}(\Pi)\log(2\mathcal{N}(\Pi,\epsilon_{\mathsf{disc}})T/\rho)}{T}} \displaystyle+\beta\epsilon_{\mathsf{disc}}\sqrt{\mathsf{SEC}(\Pi)T}
where $\mathsf{SEC}(\Pi):=\mathsf{SEC}(\Pi,r,T,\beta,V_{\mathsf{max}}^{2};\pi_{\texttt{base}})$.
Proof of Section J.2.2. For compactness, we abbreviate $\mathsf{SEC}(\Pi):=\mathsf{SEC}(\Pi,r,T,\beta,V_{\mathsf{max}}^{2};\pi_{\texttt{base}})$. From Equation (37) of Xie et al. (2024), we have

\displaystyle\frac{1}{T}\sum_{t=1}^{T}J_{\beta}(\pi^{\star}_{\beta})-J_{\beta}(\pi^{(t)}) \displaystyle\lesssim\frac{\alpha}{\beta}(R_{\mathsf{max}}+V_{\mathsf{max}})^{2}\cdot\mathsf{SEC}(\Pi)+\frac{\beta}{\alpha T}+\frac{V_{\mathsf{max}}}{T}+\frac{1}{T}\sum_{t=2}^{T}\E_{(x,y)\sim\pi_{\texttt{base}}}[\beta\log\pi^{(t)}(y\mid x)-\beta\log\pi^{\star}_{\beta}(y\mid x)] \displaystyle+\frac{\beta}{\alpha(R_{\mathsf{max}}+V_{\mathsf{max}})^{2}T}\sum_{t=2}^{T}\E_{\begin{subarray}{c}x\sim\mu\\ y,y^{\prime}\sim{\macc@depth\char 1\relax\macc@set@skewchar\macc@nested@a 111{}}^{(t)}\mid x\end{subarray}}\left[\left(\beta\log\frac{\pi^{(t)}(y\mid x)}{\pi_{\texttt{base}}(y\mid x)}-r(x,y)-\beta\log\frac{\pi^{(t)}(y^{\prime}\mid x)}{\pi_{\texttt{base}}(y^{\prime}\mid x)}+r(x,y^{\prime})\right)^{2}\right]

where ${\macc@depth\char 1\relax\macc@set@skewchar\macc@nested@a 111{}}^{(t)}:=\frac{1}{t-1}\sum_{i<t}\pi^{(i)}\otimes\pi_{\texttt{base}}$ denotes the model that, given $x\in\mathcal{X}$, samples $i\sim\mathsf{Unif}([t-1])$ and then samples $y\sim\pi^{(i)}(\cdot\mid x)$ and $y^{\prime}\sim\pi_{\texttt{base}}(\cdot\mid x)$. For any $2\leq t\leq T$, define $L^{(t)}:\Pi\to[0,\infty)$ by

\displaystyle L^{(t)}(\pi) \displaystyle:=\E_{(x,y)\sim\pi_{\texttt{base}}}[\beta\log\pi(y\mid x)-\beta\log\pi^{\star}_{\beta}(y\mid x)] \displaystyle+\frac{\beta}{\alpha(V_{\mathsf{max}}+R_{\mathsf{max}})^{2}}\E_{\begin{subarray}{c}x\sim\mu\\ y,y^{\prime}\sim{\macc@depth\char 1\relax\macc@set@skewchar\macc@nested@a 111{}}^{(t)}\mid x\end{subarray}}\left[\left(\beta\log\frac{\pi(y\mid x)}{\pi_{\texttt{base}}(y\mid x)}-r(x,y)-\beta\log\frac{\pi(y^{\prime}\mid x)}{\pi_{\texttt{base}}(y^{\prime}\mid x)}+r(x,y^{\prime})\right)^{2}\right].
Similarly, define

\displaystyle\widehat{L}^{(t)}(\pi) \displaystyle:=\sum_{(x,y,y^{\prime})\in\mathcal{D}^{(t)}}[\beta\log\pi(y^{\prime}\mid x)-\beta\log\pi^{\star}_{\beta}(y^{\prime}\mid x)] \displaystyle+\frac{\beta}{\alpha(V_{\mathsf{max}}+R_{\mathsf{max}})^{2}}\sum_{(x,y,y^{\prime})\in\mathcal{D}^{(t)}}\left[\left(\beta\log\frac{\pi(y\mid x)}{\pi_{\texttt{base}}(y\mid x)}-r(x,y)-\beta\log\frac{\pi(y^{\prime}\mid x)}{\pi_{\texttt{base}}(y^{\prime}\mid x)}+r(x,y^{\prime})\right)^{2}\right]

where $\mathcal{D}^{(t)}$ is the dataset defined in iteration $t$ of Algorithm 1. By Section J.2.1 we have $\pi^{\star}_{\beta}\in\Pi$, so $\inf_{\pi\in\Pi}\widehat{L}^{(t)}(\pi)\leq 0$. Moreover by definition, $\pi^{(t)}\in\argmin_{\pi\in\Pi}\widehat{L}^{(t)}$.

Let $\Psi$ be an $\epsilon_{\mathsf{disc}}$-net over $\Pi$, of size $\mathcal{N}(\Pi,\epsilon_{\mathsf{disc}})$. Fix any $\pi\in\Psi$ and $2\leq t\leq T$, and define increments $X_{i}:=\widehat{L}^{(i)}(\pi)-\widehat{L}^{(i-1)}(\pi)$ for $2\leq i\leq t$, with the notation $\widehat{L}^{(1)}(\pi):=0$ so that $\widehat{L}^{(t)}(\pi)=\sum_{i=2}^{t}X_{i}$. Let $\mathcal{F}_{i}$ be the filtration induced by $\mathcal{D}^{(i)}$ and define $\gamma_{i}:=\mathbb{E}[X_{i}\mid\mathcal{F}_{i-1}]$. Observe that $(t-1)L^{(t)}(\pi)=\sum_{i=2}^{t}\gamma_{i}$. For any $i$, note that we can write $X_{i}=Y_{i}+Z_{i}$ where $Y_{i}\in[-V_{\mathsf{max}},V_{\mathsf{max}}]$ and $Z_{i}\in[0,\beta/\alpha]$. By Section F.2, it holds with probability at least $1-\rho/(2|\Pi|T)$
\sum_{i=2}^{t}\mathbb{E}[Z_{i}\mid\mathcal{F}_{i-1}]\lesssim\frac{\beta}{\alpha}\log(2|\Psi|T/\rho)+\sum_{i=2}^{t}Z_{i}.
By Azuma-Hoeffding, it holds with probability at least $1-\rho/(2|\Pi|T)$ that
\sum_{i=2}^{t}\mathbb{E}[Y_{i}\mid\mathcal{F}_{i-1}]\lesssim V_{\mathsf{max}}\sqrt{T\log(2|\Psi|T/\rho)}+\sum_{i=2}^{t}Y_{i}.
Hence, with probability at least $1-\rho/(|\Psi|T)$ we have
(t-1)L^{(t)}(\pi)\lesssim\frac{\beta}{\alpha}\log(2|\Psi|T/\rho)+V_{\mathsf{max}}\sqrt{T\log(2|\Psi|T/\rho)}+\widehat{L}^{(t)}(\pi).

With probability at least $1-\rho$ this bound holds for all $\pi\in\Psi$ and $2\leq t\leq T$. Henceforth condition on this event. Fix any $\pi\in\Pi$ and $2\leq t\leq T$. Since $\Psi$ is an $\epsilon$-net for $\Pi$, we see by definition of $L^{(t)}$ that there is some $\pi^{\prime}\in\Psi$ such that

|L^{(t)}(\pi)-L^{(t)}(\pi^{\prime})|\lesssim\beta\epsilon_{\mathsf{disc}}+\frac{\beta}{\alpha(V_{\mathsf{max}}+R_{\mathsf{max}})^{2}}\cdot\beta\epsilon_{\mathsf{disc}}(V_{\mathsf{max}}+R_{\mathsf{max}})\leq\beta\epsilon_{\mathsf{disc}}\left(1+\frac{\beta}{\alpha(V_{\mathsf{max}}+R_{\mathsf{max}})}\right)
and similarly
|\widehat{L}^{(t)}(\pi)-\widehat{L}^{(t)}(\pi^{\prime})|\lesssim(t-1)\beta\epsilon_{\mathsf{disc}}\left(1+\frac{\beta}{\alpha(V_{\mathsf{max}}+R_{\mathsf{max}})}\right).
It follows that, for all $2\leq t\leq T$, since $\widehat{L}^{(t)}(\pi^{(t)})\leq 0$, we get

(t-1)L^{(t)}(\pi^{(t)})\lesssim\frac{\beta}{\alpha}\log(2|\Psi|T/\rho)+V_{\mathsf{max}}\sqrt{T\log(2|\Psi|T/\rho)}+\beta\epsilon_{\mathsf{disc}}T\left(1+\frac{\beta}{\alpha(V_{\mathsf{max}}+R_{\mathsf{max}})}\right).
Hence,

\displaystyle\frac{1}{T}\sum_{t=1}^{T}J_{\beta}(\pi^{\star}_{\beta})-J_{\beta}(\pi^{(t)}) \displaystyle\lesssim\frac{\alpha}{\beta}(R_{\mathsf{max}}+V_{\mathsf{max}})^{2}\cdot\mathsf{SEC}(\Pi)+\frac{\beta}{\alpha T}+\frac{V_{\mathsf{max}}}{T}+\frac{1}{T}\sum_{t=2}^{T}L^{(t)}(\pi^{(t)}) \displaystyle\lesssim(R_{\mathsf{max}}+V_{\mathsf{max}})\sqrt{\frac{\mathsf{SEC}(\Pi)\log(2|\Psi|T/\rho)}{T}}+\beta\epsilon_{\mathsf{disc}}\sqrt{\mathsf{SEC}(\Pi)T}
by taking
\alpha:=\frac{\beta}{R_{\mathsf{max}}+V_{\mathsf{max}}}\sqrt{\frac{\log(2|\Psi|T/\rho)}{\mathsf{SEC}(\Pi)T}}.

Since the output $\widehat{\pi}$ of Algorithm 1 satisfies $\widehat{\pi}\in\argmax_{t\in[T]}J_{\beta}(\pi^{(t)})$, the claimed bound on $J_{\beta}(\pi^{\star}_{\beta})-J_{\beta}(\widehat{\pi})$ is immediate. Finally, observe that by definition of $\pi^{\star}_{\beta}$,

\displaystyle J_{\beta}(\pi^{\star}_{\beta})-J_{\beta}(\widehat{\pi}) \displaystyle=\E_{(x,y)\sim\pi^{\star}_{\beta}}\left[r(x,y)-\beta\log\frac{\pi^{\star}_{\beta}(y\mid x)}{\pi_{\texttt{base}}(y\mid x)}\right]-\E_{(x,y)\sim\widehat{\pi}}\left[r(x,y)-\beta\log\frac{\widehat{\pi}(y\mid x)}{\pi_{\texttt{base}}(y\mid x)}\right] \displaystyle=\E_{(x,y)\sim\pi^{\star}_{\beta}}\left[r(x,y)-\beta\log\frac{\pi^{\star}_{\beta}(y\mid x)}{\pi_{\texttt{base}}(y\mid x)}\right]-\E_{(x,y)\sim\widehat{\pi}}\left[r(x,y)-\beta\log\frac{\pi^{\star}_{\beta}(y\mid x)}{\pi_{\texttt{base}}(y\mid x)}\right] \displaystyle\qquad+\E_{(x,y)\sim\widehat{\pi}}\left[\beta\log\frac{\widehat{\pi}(y\mid x)}{\pi^{\star}_{\beta}(y\mid x)}\right] \displaystyle=\beta\log\E_{(x,y)\sim\pi_{\texttt{base}}}[\exp(r(x,y))]-\beta\log\E_{(x,y)\sim\pi_{\texttt{base}}}[\exp(r(x,y))]+\beta D_{\mathsf{KL}}\left(\widehat{\pi}\,\|\,\pi^{\star}_{\beta}\right) \displaystyle=\beta D_{\mathsf{KL}}\left(\widehat{\pi}\,\|\,\pi^{\star}_{\beta}\right).
This completes the proof. ∎

sections.text:
Algorithm 1 Reward-based variant of Exploratory Preference Optimization (Xie et al., 2024)

input: Base model $\pi_{\texttt{base}}:\mathcal{X}\to\Delta(\mathcal{Y})$, reward function $r:\mathcal{X}\times\mathcal{Y}\to\mathbb{R}$, number of iterations $T\in\mathbb{N}$, KL regularization coefficient $\beta>0$, optimism coefficient $\alpha>0$.
Initialize: $\pi^{(1)}\leftarrow\pi_{\texttt{base}}$, $\mathcal{D}^{(0)}\leftarrow\varnothing$.
for iteration $t=1,\dots,T$ do
Generate sample: $(x^{(t)},y^{(t)},\widetilde{y}^{(t)})$ via $x^{(t)}\sim\mu$, $y^{(t)}\sim\pi^{(t)}(\cdot\mid x^{(t)})$, $\widetilde{y}^{(t)}\sim\pi_{\texttt{base}}(\cdot\mid x^{(t)})$.
Update dataset: $\mathcal{D}^{(t)}\leftarrow\mathcal{D}^{(t-1)}\cup\{(x^{(t)},y^{(t)},\widetilde{y}^{(t)})\}$.
Model optimization with global optimism: $\displaystyle\pi^{(t+1)}$ $\displaystyle\leftarrow\argmin_{\pi\in\Pi}\Bigg\{\alpha\sum_{(x,y,y^{\prime})\in\mathcal{D}^{(t)}}\log(\pi(y^{\prime}\mid x))$ (205) $\displaystyle-\sum_{(x,y,y^{\prime})\in\mathcal{D}^{(t)}}\left(\beta\log\frac{\pi(y\mid x)}{\pi_{\texttt{base}}(y\mid x)}-\beta\log\frac{\pi(y^{\prime}\mid x)}{\pi_{\texttt{base}}(y^{\prime}\mid x)}-(r(x,y)-r(x,y^{\prime}))\right)^{2}\Bigg\}.$ (206)
return: $\widehat{\pi}\leftarrow\argmax_{t\in[T+1]}J_{\beta}(\pi^{(t)})$. $\triangleright$ Can estimate $J_{\beta}(\pi^{(t)})$ using validation data.

In this section, we give self-contained guarantees for the XPO algorithm (Algorithm 1). XPO was introduced in Xie et al. (2024) for KL-regularized policy optimization in the related setting where the learner only has indirect access to the reward function $r$ through preference data (specifically, pairs of actions labeled via a Bradley-Terry model). Standard offline algorithms for this problem, such as DPO, require bounds on concentrability of the model class (see e.g. Eq. 22). Xie et al. (2024) show that the XPO algorithm avoids this dependence, and instead requires bounded Sequential Extrapolation Coefficient.

Algorithm 1 is a variant of the XPO algorithm which is adapted to reward-based feedback (as opposed to preference-based feedback), and Section J.2.2 shows that this algorithm enjoys guarantees similar to those of Xie et al. (2024) for this setting. Note that this is not an immediate corollary of the results in Xie et al. (2024), since the sample complexity in the preference-based setting scales with $e^{O(R_{\mathsf{max}})}$, and for our application to sharpening it is important to avoid this dependence. However, our algorithm and analysis only diverge from Xie et al. (2024) in a few places.

[Variant of Xie et al. (2024, Theorem 3.1)] Suppose that Sections J.2.1 and J.2.1 hold. For any $T\in\mathbb{N}$, $\epsilon_{\mathsf{disc}},\rho\in(0,1)$, by setting $\alpha:=\frac{\beta}{R_{\mathsf{max}}+V_{\mathsf{max}}}\sqrt{\frac{\log(2\mathcal{N}(\Pi,\epsilon_{\mathsf{disc}})T/\rho)}{\mathsf{SEC}(\Pi)T}}$, Algorithm 1 produces a model $\widehat{\pi}\in\Pi$ such that with probability at least $1-\rho$,

\displaystyle\beta D_{\mathsf{KL}}\left(\widehat{\pi}\,\|\,\pi^{\star}_{\beta}\right)=J_{\beta}(\pi^{\star}_{\beta})-J_{\beta}(\widehat{\pi}) \displaystyle\lesssim(R_{\mathsf{max}}+V_{\mathsf{max}})\sqrt{\frac{\mathsf{SEC}(\Pi)\log(2\mathcal{N}(\Pi,\epsilon_{\mathsf{disc}})T/\rho)}{T}} \displaystyle+\beta\epsilon_{\mathsf{disc}}\sqrt{\mathsf{SEC}(\Pi)T}

where $\mathsf{SEC}(\Pi):=\mathsf{SEC}(\Pi,r,T,\beta,V_{\mathsf{max}}^{2};\pi_{\texttt{base}})$.

Proof of Section J.2.2. For compactness, we abbreviate $\mathsf{SEC}(\Pi):=\mathsf{SEC}(\Pi,r,T,\beta,V_{\mathsf{max}}^{2};\pi_{\texttt{base}})$. From Equation (37) of Xie et al. (2024), we have

\displaystyle\frac{1}{T}\sum_{t=1}^{T}J_{\beta}(\pi^{\star}_{\beta})-J_{\beta}(\pi^{(t)}) \displaystyle\lesssim\frac{\alpha}{\beta}(R_{\mathsf{max}}+V_{\mathsf{max}})^{2}\cdot\mathsf{SEC}(\Pi)+\frac{\beta}{\alpha T}+\frac{V_{\mathsf{max}}}{T}+\frac{1}{T}\sum_{t=2}^{T}\E_{(x,y)\sim\pi_{\texttt{base}}}[\beta\log\pi^{(t)}(y\mid x)-\beta\log\pi^{\star}_{\beta}(y\mid x)] \displaystyle+\frac{\beta}{\alpha(R_{\mathsf{max}}+V_{\mathsf{max}})^{2}T}\sum_{t=2}^{T}\E_{\begin{subarray}{c}x\sim\mu\\ y,y^{\prime}\sim{\macc@depth\char 1\relax\macc@set@skewchar\macc@nested@a 111{}}^{(t)}\mid x\end{subarray}}\left[\left(\beta\log\frac{\pi^{(t)}(y\mid x)}{\pi_{\texttt{base}}(y\mid x)}-r(x,y)-\beta\log\frac{\pi^{(t)}(y^{\prime}\mid x)}{\pi_{\texttt{base}}(y^{\prime}\mid x)}+r(x,y^{\prime})\right)^{2}\right]

where ${\macc@depth\char 1\relax\macc@set@skewchar\macc@nested@a 111{}}^{(t)}:=\frac{1}{t-1}\sum_{i<t}\pi^{(i)}\otimes\pi_{\texttt{base}}$ denotes the model that, given $x\in\mathcal{X}$, samples $i\sim\mathsf{Unif}([t-1])$ and then samples $y\sim\pi^{(i)}(\cdot\mid x)$ and $y^{\prime}\sim\pi_{\texttt{base}}(\cdot\mid x)$. For any $2\leq t\leq T$, define $L^{(t)}:\Pi\to[0,\infty)$ by

\displaystyle L^{(t)}(\pi) \displaystyle:=\E_{(x,y)\sim\pi_{\texttt{base}}}[\beta\log\pi(y\mid x)-\beta\log\pi^{\star}_{\beta}(y\mid x)] \displaystyle+\frac{\beta}{\alpha(V_{\mathsf{max}}+R_{\mathsf{max}})^{2}}\E_{\begin{subarray}{c}x\sim\mu\\ y,y^{\prime}\sim{\macc@depth\char 1\relax\macc@set@skewchar\macc@nested@a 111{}}^{(t)}\mid x\end{subarray}}\left[\left(\beta\log\frac{\pi(y\mid x)}{\pi_{\texttt{base}}(y\mid x)}-r(x,y)-\beta\log\frac{\pi(y^{\prime}\mid x)}{\pi_{\texttt{base}}(y^{\prime}\mid x)}+r(x,y^{\prime})\right)^{2}\right].

Similarly, define

\displaystyle\widehat{L}^{(t)}(\pi) \displaystyle:=\sum_{(x,y,y^{\prime})\in\mathcal{D}^{(t)}}[\beta\log\pi(y^{\prime}\mid x)-\beta\log\pi^{\star}_{\beta}(y^{\prime}\mid x)] \displaystyle+\frac{\beta}{\alpha(V_{\mathsf{max}}+R_{\mathsf{max}})^{2}}\sum_{(x,y,y^{\prime})\in\mathcal{D}^{(t)}}\left[\left(\beta\log\frac{\pi(y\mid x)}{\pi_{\texttt{base}}(y\mid x)}-r(x,y)-\beta\log\frac{\pi(y^{\prime}\mid x)}{\pi_{\texttt{base}}(y^{\prime}\mid x)}+r(x,y^{\prime})\right)^{2}\right]

where $\mathcal{D}^{(t)}$ is the dataset defined in iteration $t$ of Algorithm 1. By Section J.2.1 we have $\pi^{\star}_{\beta}\in\Pi$, so $\inf_{\pi\in\Pi}\widehat{L}^{(t)}(\pi)\leq 0$. Moreover by definition, $\pi^{(t)}\in\argmin_{\pi\in\Pi}\widehat{L}^{(t)}$.

Let $\Psi$ be an $\epsilon_{\mathsf{disc}}$-net over $\Pi$, of size $\mathcal{N}(\Pi,\epsilon_{\mathsf{disc}})$. Fix any $\pi\in\Psi$ and $2\leq t\leq T$, and define increments $X_{i}:=\widehat{L}^{(i)}(\pi)-\widehat{L}^{(i-1)}(\pi)$ for $2\leq i\leq t$, with the notation $\widehat{L}^{(1)}(\pi):=0$ so that $\widehat{L}^{(t)}(\pi)=\sum_{i=2}^{t}X_{i}$. Let $\mathcal{F}_{i}$ be the filtration induced by $\mathcal{D}^{(i)}$ and define $\gamma_{i}:=\mathbb{E}[X_{i}\mid\mathcal{F}_{i-1}]$. Observe that $(t-1)L^{(t)}(\pi)=\sum_{i=2}^{t}\gamma_{i}$. For any $i$, note that we can write $X_{i}=Y_{i}+Z_{i}$ where $Y_{i}\in[-V_{\mathsf{max}},V_{\mathsf{max}}]$ and $Z_{i}\in[0,\beta/\alpha]$. By Section F.2, it holds with probability at least $1-\rho/(2|\Pi|T)$

\sum_{i=2}^{t}\mathbb{E}[Z_{i}\mid\mathcal{F}_{i-1}]\lesssim\frac{\beta}{\alpha}\log(2|\Psi|T/\rho)+\sum_{i=2}^{t}Z_{i}.

By Azuma-Hoeffding, it holds with probability at least $1-\rho/(2|\Pi|T)$ that

\sum_{i=2}^{t}\mathbb{E}[Y_{i}\mid\mathcal{F}_{i-1}]\lesssim V_{\mathsf{max}}\sqrt{T\log(2|\Psi|T/\rho)}+\sum_{i=2}^{t}Y_{i}.

Hence, with probability at least $1-\rho/(|\Psi|T)$ we have

(t-1)L^{(t)}(\pi)\lesssim\frac{\beta}{\alpha}\log(2|\Psi|T/\rho)+V_{\mathsf{max}}\sqrt{T\log(2|\Psi|T/\rho)}+\widehat{L}^{(t)}(\pi).

With probability at least $1-\rho$ this bound holds for all $\pi\in\Psi$ and $2\leq t\leq T$. Henceforth condition on this event. Fix any $\pi\in\Pi$ and $2\leq t\leq T$. Since $\Psi$ is an $\epsilon$-net for $\Pi$, we see by definition of $L^{(t)}$ that there is some $\pi^{\prime}\in\Psi$ such that

|L^{(t)}(\pi)-L^{(t)}(\pi^{\prime})|\lesssim\beta\epsilon_{\mathsf{disc}}+\frac{\beta}{\alpha(V_{\mathsf{max}}+R_{\mathsf{max}})^{2}}\cdot\beta\epsilon_{\mathsf{disc}}(V_{\mathsf{max}}+R_{\mathsf{max}})\leq\beta\epsilon_{\mathsf{disc}}\left(1+\frac{\beta}{\alpha(V_{\mathsf{max}}+R_{\mathsf{max}})}\right)

and similarly

|\widehat{L}^{(t)}(\pi)-\widehat{L}^{(t)}(\pi^{\prime})|\lesssim(t-1)\beta\epsilon_{\mathsf{disc}}\left(1+\frac{\beta}{\alpha(V_{\mathsf{max}}+R_{\mathsf{max}})}\right).

It follows that, for all $2\leq t\leq T$, since $\widehat{L}^{(t)}(\pi^{(t)})\leq 0$, we get

(t-1)L^{(t)}(\pi^{(t)})\lesssim\frac{\beta}{\alpha}\log(2|\Psi|T/\rho)+V_{\mathsf{max}}\sqrt{T\log(2|\Psi|T/\rho)}+\beta\epsilon_{\mathsf{disc}}T\left(1+\frac{\beta}{\alpha(V_{\mathsf{max}}+R_{\mathsf{max}})}\right).

Hence,

\displaystyle\frac{1}{T}\sum_{t=1}^{T}J_{\beta}(\pi^{\star}_{\beta})-J_{\beta}(\pi^{(t)}) \displaystyle\lesssim\frac{\alpha}{\beta}(R_{\mathsf{max}}+V_{\mathsf{max}})^{2}\cdot\mathsf{SEC}(\Pi)+\frac{\beta}{\alpha T}+\frac{V_{\mathsf{max}}}{T}+\frac{1}{T}\sum_{t=2}^{T}L^{(t)}(\pi^{(t)}) \displaystyle\lesssim(R_{\mathsf{max}}+V_{\mathsf{max}})\sqrt{\frac{\mathsf{SEC}(\Pi)\log(2|\Psi|T/\rho)}{T}}+\beta\epsilon_{\mathsf{disc}}\sqrt{\mathsf{SEC}(\Pi)T}

by taking

\alpha:=\frac{\beta}{R_{\mathsf{max}}+V_{\mathsf{max}}}\sqrt{\frac{\log(2|\Psi|T/\rho)}{\mathsf{SEC}(\Pi)T}}.

Since the output $\widehat{\pi}$ of Algorithm 1 satisfies $\widehat{\pi}\in\argmax_{t\in[T]}J_{\beta}(\pi^{(t)})$, the claimed bound on $J_{\beta}(\pi^{\star}_{\beta})-J_{\beta}(\widehat{\pi})$ is immediate. Finally, observe that by definition of $\pi^{\star}_{\beta}$,

\displaystyle J_{\beta}(\pi^{\star}_{\beta})-J_{\beta}(\widehat{\pi}) \displaystyle=\E_{(x,y)\sim\pi^{\star}_{\beta}}\left[r(x,y)-\beta\log\frac{\pi^{\star}_{\beta}(y\mid x)}{\pi_{\texttt{base}}(y\mid x)}\right]-\E_{(x,y)\sim\widehat{\pi}}\left[r(x,y)-\beta\log\frac{\widehat{\pi}(y\mid x)}{\pi_{\texttt{base}}(y\mid x)}\right] \displaystyle=\E_{(x,y)\sim\pi^{\star}_{\beta}}\left[r(x,y)-\beta\log\frac{\pi^{\star}_{\beta}(y\mid x)}{\pi_{\texttt{base}}(y\mid x)}\right]-\E_{(x,y)\sim\widehat{\pi}}\left[r(x,y)-\beta\log\frac{\pi^{\star}_{\beta}(y\mid x)}{\pi_{\texttt{base}}(y\mid x)}\right] \displaystyle\qquad+\E_{(x,y)\sim\widehat{\pi}}\left[\beta\log\frac{\widehat{\pi}(y\mid x)}{\pi^{\star}_{\beta}(y\mid x)}\right] \displaystyle=\beta\log\E_{(x,y)\sim\pi_{\texttt{base}}}[\exp(r(x,y))]-\beta\log\E_{(x,y)\sim\pi_{\texttt{base}}}[\exp(r(x,y))]+\beta D_{\mathsf{KL}}\left(\widehat{\pi}\,\|\,\pi^{\star}_{\beta}\right) \displaystyle=\beta D_{\mathsf{KL}}\left(\widehat{\pi}\,\|\,\pi^{\star}_{\beta}\right).

This completes the proof. ∎

J.2.3 Applying XPO to maximum-likelihood sharpening

paragraphs.text: We now prove Section J.2.3, the formal statement of Section 4.2.2, which applies XPO to maximum-likelihood sharpening. This result is a straightforward corollary of Section J.2.2 with the reward function $r_{\texttt{self}}(x,y):=\log\pi_{\texttt{base}}(y\mid x)$, together with the observation that low KL-regularized regret implies sharpness (under Section 4.2).

[Sharpening via active exploration] There are absolute constants $c_{\mathrm{\ref{thm:xpo-sharpening-apx}}},C_{\mathrm{\ref{thm:xpo-sharpening-apx}}}>0$ so that the following holds. Let $\epsilon,\delta,\gamma_{\mathsf{margin}},\rho,\beta\in(0,1)$ and $T\in\mathbb{N}$ be given. For base model $\pi_{\texttt{base}}$, define reward function $r(x,y):=\log\pi_{\texttt{base}}(y\mid x)$. Let $R_{\mathsf{max}}\geq 1+\max_{x,y}\log\frac{1}{\pi_{\texttt{base}}(y\mid x)}$. Suppose that $\pi_{\texttt{base}}$ satisfies Section 4.2 with parameter $\gamma_{\mathsf{margin}}$, that $\beta^{-1}\geq 2\gamma_{\mathsf{margin}}^{-1}\log(2|\mathcal{Y}|/\delta)$, and that there is $\epsilon_{\mathsf{disc}}\in(0,1)$ so that
T\geq C_{\mathrm{\ref{thm:xpo-sharpening-apx}}}\frac{R_{\mathsf{max}}^{2}\mathsf{SEC}(\Pi)\log(2\mathcal{N}(\Pi,\epsilon_{\mathsf{disc}})T/\rho)}{\epsilon^{2}\delta^{2}\beta^{2}}
and
\epsilon_{\mathsf{disc}}\leq c_{\mathrm{\ref{thm:xpo-sharpening-apx}}}\frac{\epsilon\delta}{\sqrt{\mathsf{SEC}(\Pi)T}}

where $\mathsf{SEC}(\Pi):=\mathsf{SEC}(\Pi,r,T,\beta,R_{\mathsf{max}}^{2};\pi_{\texttt{base}})$. Also suppose that $\pi^{\star}_{\beta}\in\Pi$ where $\pi^{\star}_{\beta}(y\mid x)\propto\pi_{\texttt{base}}^{1+\beta^{-1}}(y\mid x)$.

Then applying Algorithm 1 with base model $\pi_{\texttt{base}}$, reward function $r$, iteration count $T$, regularization $\beta$, and optimism parameter $\alpha:=\frac{\beta}{R_{\mathsf{max}}}\sqrt{\frac{\log(2\mathcal{N}(\Pi,\epsilon_{\mathsf{disc}})T/\delta)}{\mathsf{SEC}(\Pi)T}}$ yields a model $\widehat{\pi}\in\Pi$ such that with probability at least $1-\rho$,
\mathbb{P}_{x\sim\mu}[\widehat{\pi}(\bm{y}^{\star}(x)\mid x)<1-\delta]\leq\epsilon.
The total sample complexity is

m=\widetilde{O}\left(\frac{R_{\mathsf{max}}^{2}\mathsf{SEC}(\Pi)\log(\mathcal{N}(\Pi,\epsilon_{\mathsf{disc}})/\rho)\log^{2}(\lvert\mathcal{Y}\rvert\delta^{-1})}{\gamma_{\mathsf{margin}}^{2}\epsilon^{2}\delta^{2}}\right).

Proof of Section J.2.3. By definition of $r$, we have $|r(x,y)|\leq R_{\mathsf{max}}$ for all $x,y$. By assumption, Section J.2.1 is satisfied, and by definition of $R_{\mathsf{max}}$, Section 4.2.2 is satisfied with parameter $V_{\mathsf{max}}:=\beta R_{\mathsf{max}}\leq R_{\mathsf{max}}$. It follows from Section J.2.2 that with probability at least $1-\rho$, the output $\widehat{\pi}$ of Algorithm 1 satisfies

\displaystyle\beta D_{\mathsf{KL}}\left(\widehat{\pi}\,\|\,\pi^{\star}_{\beta}\right) \displaystyle\lesssim(R_{\mathsf{max}}+V_{\mathsf{max}})\sqrt{\frac{\mathsf{SEC}(\Pi)\log(2\mathcal{N}(\Pi,\epsilon_{\mathsf{disc}})T/\rho)}{T}} \displaystyle\qquad+\beta\epsilon_{\mathsf{disc}}\sqrt{\mathsf{SEC}(\Pi)T}.

By choice of $T$ and $\epsilon_{\mathsf{disc}}$, so long as $C_{\mathrm{\ref{thm:xpo-sharpening-apx}}}>0$ is chosen to be a sufficiently large constant and $c_{\mathrm{\ref{thm:xpo-sharpening-apx}}}>0$ is chosen to be a sufficiently small constant, we have $\beta D_{\mathsf{KL}}\left(\widehat{\pi}\,\|\,\pi^{\star}_{\beta}\right)\leq\frac{1}{12}\beta\epsilon\delta$, so by e.g. Equation (16) of Sason and Verdú (2016), $D^{2}_{\mathsf{H}}\left(\widehat{\pi},\pi^{\star}_{\beta}\right)\leq\epsilon\delta/(12)$.
For any $x\in\mathcal{X}$ and $y^{\prime}\in\mathcal{Y}\setminus\bm{y}^{\star}(x)$, by Section 4.2 and definition of $\pi^{\star}_{\beta}$ we have

\displaystyle\frac{1}{\pi^{\star}_{\beta}(y^{\prime}\mid x)}\geq\frac{\max_{y\in\mathcal{Y}}\pi^{\star}_{\beta}(y\mid x)}{\pi^{\star}_{\beta}(y^{\prime}\mid x)} \displaystyle=\left(\frac{\max_{y\in\mathcal{Y}}\pi_{\texttt{base}}(y\mid x)}{\pi_{\texttt{base}}(y^{\prime}\mid x)}\right)^{1+\beta^{-1}} \displaystyle\geq(1+\gamma_{\mathsf{margin}})^{1+\beta^{-1}}\geq e^{\gamma_{\mathsf{margin}}/(2\beta)}\geq\frac{2|\mathcal{Y}|}{\delta}
where the final inequality is by the assumption on $\beta$ in the theorem statement. Therefore
\pi^{\star}_{\beta}(\bm{y}^{\star}(x)\mid x)\geq 1-\sum_{y^{\prime}\in\mathcal{Y}\setminus\bm{y}^{\star}(x)}\pi^{\star}_{\beta}(y^{\prime}\mid x)\geq 1-\frac{\delta}{2}.
Now for any $x$, we can lower bound

\displaystyle D^{2}_{\mathsf{H}}\left(\widehat{\pi}(\cdot\mid x),\pi^{\star}_{\beta}(\cdot\mid x)\right) \displaystyle\geq\left(\sqrt{1-\widehat{\pi}(\bm{y}^{\star}(x)\mid x)}-\sqrt{1-\pi^{\star}_{\beta}(\bm{y}^{\star}(x)\mid x)}\right)^{2} \displaystyle\geq\frac{\delta}{12}\cdot\mathbb{I}\{\widehat{\pi}(y^{\star}(x)\mid x)\leq 1-\delta\}.
Hence,

\displaystyle\mathbb{P}_{x\sim\mu}[\widehat{\pi}(\bm{y}^{\star}(x)\mid x)<1-\delta] \displaystyle\leq\frac{12}{\delta}\mathbb{E}_{x\sim\mu}D^{2}_{\mathsf{H}}\left(\widehat{\pi}(\cdot\mid x),\pi^{\star}_{\beta}(\cdot\mid x)\right) \displaystyle=\frac{12}{\delta}D^{2}_{\mathsf{H}}\left(\widehat{\pi},\pi^{\star}_{\beta}\right) \displaystyle\leq\epsilon.
as claimed. ∎
